It won't be wrong to say that something which was meant only for special occasions is now becoming a symbol of luxury and personal style. Luxury brands are designing brooches as collectible pieces, using rare gemstones and fine craftsmanship, much like watches or fine jewellery.  For men, wearing a brooch shows confidence and attention to detail, instantly elevating an outfit. With fashion becoming more expressive and gender-fluid, brooches are no longer just accessories, they are turning into statement pieces and valuable additions to a modern luxury wardrobe.  - Ends  Published By: Mehak Malhotra Published On: Feb 12, 2026

title: Chandrayaan-4 eyes Moon's Mons Mouton: Why this landing site is not ordinary
text: India’s planned Chandrayaan-4 mission, designed to bring lunar samples back to Earth, may target the Mons Mouton region near the Moon’s south pole, an area scientists consider one of the most scientifically valuable locations on the lunar surface.  If the landing site is confirmed, the mission would mark India’s first attempt at lunar sample return, a major step beyond the successful soft-landing achieved by Chandrayaan-3 in 2023.  advertisement  Isro recently released a new scientific study based on high-resolution imagery from India’s lunar orbiter that analysed four potential landing sites in the region.  WHAT IS MOON'S MONS MUTON REGION?  Mons Mouton is a mountainous highland located near the lunar south polar region, an area believed to hold clues about the Moon’s early geological history.  The region sits close to permanently shadowed craters, where temperatures remain extremely low and water-ice deposits may be preserved for billions of years.  These icy reserves are considered crucial for future human exploration because they could provide drinking water, oxygen, and even rocket fuel.  Scientists believe Mons Mouton is especially valuable because it exposes ancient lunar crustal material, possibly dating back more than four billion years.  WHY CHANDRAYAAN-4 IS CRITICAL FOR ISRO?  Collecting and returning samples from such terrain could help researchers better understand how the Moon, and by extension, Earth, formed in the early solar system.  While previous missions from the United States, the former Soviet Union, and China have returned lunar samples, no mission has yet brought back material from the Moon’s south polar highlands.  For the Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro), targeting this region is both a scientific and technological milestone. The terrain near Mons Mouton is rugged, uneven, and filled with deep shadows, making landing operations significantly more complex than missions to equatorial regions of the Moon.  Successfully landing and retrieving samples from this environment would demonstrate India’s growing capability in precision landing, robotic sampling, launch coordination, and Earth-return technology.  Chandrayaan-4 is expected to involve multiple spacecraft components, including a lander, rover, ascent module, and an Earth-return module, making it one of Isro’s most complex missions to date. Landing site of Chandrayaan-3. (Photo: Isro)  The ability to collect and safely return lunar material would place India among a small group of nations that have mastered end-to-end sample-return missions, widely regarded as a benchmark of deep-space capability.  advertisement  Beyond national prestige, samples from Mons Mouton could reshape scientific understanding of water distribution on the Moon and the evolution of the lunar south pole environment.  These findings may also guide future international missions and potential human bases in the polar region.  If successful, Chandrayaan-4 would not just revisit the Moon, it would bring a piece of it home, marking a defining moment in India’s expanding space ambitions.  - Ends  Published By: Sibu Kumar Tripathi Published On: Feb 12, 2026

title: Trade deal: Trump may cut tariffs on textiles to zero. But there's a catch
text: A day after the Trump administration revised its US-India trade deal factsheet, walking back on certain terms, more concessions are likely in store for New Delhi. Union Minister Piyush Goyal, on Thursday, in a big reveal, said India would also receive textile-related trade benefits similar to those extended to Bangladesh by the US. The minister, who has been at the forefront of trade negotiations with the US, suggested that, like Bangladesh, Indian textiles are also expected to get zero-tariff access to the US on garments made using American cotton once the final deal is signed.  advertisement  The revelation by Goyal will come as a shot in the arm for India's textile and apparel exporters after the US-Bangladesh trade deal posed fresh challenges to the sensitive industry. In essence, the US seems to be slowly removing the trade deal irritants as it resets its overall bilateral ties with India.  Goyal's clarification came amid the political sparring over the trade deal after Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said the agreement was a "wholesale surrender" to Trump.  TRADE DEAL: WHAT PIYUSH GOYAL SAID?  Hitting out at the Leader of the Opposition, Goyal said, "He spread another lie in the Parliament that Bangladesh has got more benefits from the trade (deal) than India."  "Just as Bangladesh has a facility that if raw material is purchased from America, then if you process it and make cloth and export it, then it will be available at zero reciprocal tariff. India also has the same facility, and India will also get it," the Commerce Minister said.  Goyal said that while this clause might not be in the interim trade deal framework, released by the countries last week, it would feature in the final agreement.  "Right now, our framework agreement is being made. When the interim agreement is finalised, then you will get to see this in the fine print," he emphasised.  Now, as per the latest pact, India has already offered duty concessions for imports of US extra-long staple cotton. However, unlike Bangladesh, India has so far not secured zero-duty access for finished garments made using US cotton.  WHAT DOES IT MEAN FOR INDIA'S TEXTILES SECTOR?  If India eventually manages to reach such an agreement with the US, it will come as a welcome relief for India's labour-intensive textile sector. Notably, the US is the top market for India's textile exports, and 30% of all textile and apparel shipments from the country reach American shores.  Last week, the textile exporters rejoiced after India and the US reached a trade deal, with Trump reducing tariffs to 18% from a crippling 50%. Crucially, it gave India a tariff advantage over its competitors like Bangladesh, Pakistan (19%), Vietnam (20%) and China (30%).  The gains vanished days later after Bangladesh struck a trade deal with the US, which cut duties on exports to 19% from 20%. However, what pinched India was the zero-duty clause on Bangladeshi garment exports made with US cotton.  advertisement  Under it, Bangladeshi garments and apparel made using American cotton will face zero duties. Thus, if Indian textiles face 18% tariff, it loses the competitive advantage as Bangladeshi garments will be cheaper for US consumers.  THE COTTON CLAUSE  Moreover, to get zero-tariff access to the US, Bangladesh would have to make more garments using American cotton. Thus, it will have to import more of this cotton and reduce dependence on its present suppliers.  Presently, India accounts for Bangladesh's top three importers of cotton. Now, as part of the trade deal with the US, Bangladesh is likely to shift even more towards American cotton. It will put pressure on Indian cotton traders.  Now, if India does manage to get such a concession from the Trump administration, like Bangladesh, it will go a long way in easing concerns within the domestic textile industry.  It comes even as the Trump administration revised its factsheet on the India-US trade deal. The White House dropped the claim that India would reduce tariffs on "certain pulses" and changed the wording relating to the $500 billion purchase proposal. Moreover, the mention of India "removing" its digital services tax or Google tax was dropped altogether.  Are more such trade concessions and sweeteners from Trump in store before the mid-March signing of the formal deal? The next few weeks will give an indication. Thanks for your attention to this article!  - Ends  Published By: Abhishek De Published On: Feb 12, 2026  Tune In

title: Kanpur tycoon's son arrested in Lamborghini crash case, cops say he was driving
text: Four days after crashing his Lamborghini in Kanpur, tobacco tycoon KK Mishra's son, Shivam Mishra, was arrested on Thursday. Police have said that Shivam was driving the high-end luxury vehicle at the time of the accident. Cops have sought a 14-day remand of Shivam.  Speaking to reporters after Shivam Mishra’s arrest, DCP Central Kanpur Atul Kumar Srivastava said police had received specific inputs about his presence in the city following which five teams were constituted to track him down.  advertisement  He added that the investigation has confirmed that Mishra was behind the wheel of the Lamborghini at the time of the accident, even as police had been working to trace him in the days after the crash.  #WATCH | Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh: Lamborghini car accident case | DCP Central Kanpur Atul Kumar Srivastava says, "We got information that he (Shivam Mishra) is in Kanpur. Five teams were formed, and we have arrested him, and he has been presented in court. In the investigation, it pic.twitter.com/gkfsB32kr3 — ANI (@ANI) February 12, 2026  Shivam was taken for a routine medical checkup before being presented before the court. Visuals which surfaced shortly after Shivam's arrest showed him limping and leaning on police personnel and others for support as he was escorted for the medical check-up.  During court hearing, the officials said that Shivam was arrested for non co-operation in the investigation and evading police. Accused Shivam Mishra, 35, was taken to a Kanpur court after arrest.  The accident occurred around 3 pm on VIP Road, when a speeding Lamborghini Revuelto, a luxury Italian sports car priced at over Rs 10 crore, ploughed into pedestrians and other vehicles before coming to a halt after mounting a divider.  An FIR was later filed by one of the injured, 18-year-old e-rickshaw driver Mohd Taufeeq.  The case took a dramatic turn a day earlier when a man identified as Mohan, claiming to be the designated driver, said "he and not Shivam was behind the wheel at the time of the crash". Speaking to reporters outside a court, Mohan alleged that Shivam, seated beside him, suffered a sudden seizure moments before the impact.  "I was driving when he suddenly collapsed on me. I panicked and tried to hold him with one hand. The car first hit a three-wheeler, climbed the divider and then stopped," Mohan said. He also claimed the vehicle's automatic locking system delayed his exit, after which he shifted Shivam to the driver's seat and stepped out.  Mohan's lawyer moved a surrender application before the court, and he appeared on Wednesday to formally surrender. However, the Gwaltoli police, in their report, did not name him as an accused. Taking note of the police stand, the court refused to accept his surrender and sought a detailed report from the local police station.  All this happened while Shivam was on the run.  Despite the claim, police said the evidence pointed squarely at Shivam. Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal said CCTV footage, eyewitness accounts and other material show Shivam was driving when the Lamborghini rammed into people and vehicles.  Senior officers also cited videos allegedly showing bystanders pulling a man believed to be Shivam from the driver's seat immediately after the crash.  Initially, the FIR was registered against an unidentified driver but was later amended to name Shivam as the accused. The supercar has been seized for forensic examination.  advertisement  The defence has also claimed that the complainant no longer wants to pursue the case. Shivam's lawyer, Dharmendra Singh, said Taufeeq had reached a mutual settlement and did not wish to initiate legal action. He further alleged that Mohan was driving and paid compensation for the victim's medical treatment and losses.  Sources said Taufeeq was called to the Gwaltoli police station on the day of the crash itself, where a written settlement was signed in the presence of then station house officer Santosh Kumar Gaur. The SHO was later removed from charge and sent to lines, though senior officials declined to comment on the alleged settlement.  Shivam's father had earlier told police that a driver was at the wheel. He later modified his stand, saying he did not know who was driving and the matter required investigation. He also claimed the car had developed a technical snag a day earlier and was taken out for a test drive after repairs.  According to KK Mishra, Shivam began losing consciousness while returning from Civil Lines, after which the driver slowed down and an autorickshaw struck the car. Security personnel in an accompanying SUV allegedly broke the window to rescue him.  The family has maintained that Shivam suffers from epilepsy and is undergoing treatment in Delhi, while denying allegations of speeding or intoxication. Police, however, have rejected those claims, reiterating that technical and visual evidence places Shivam behind the wheel at the time of the crash.  - Ends  Published By: Karishma Saurabh Kalita Published On: Feb 12, 2026  Tune In

title: Microsoft AI boss Mustafa Suleyman says AI will replace most white-collar jobs in 12 months
text: Microsoft AI boss Mustafa Suleyman has warned that AI could be coming to take most white-collar jobs soon. Not just coders, but even professionals such as lawyers and accountants, may see their job be automated by AI.  In an interview with the Financial Times, Suleyman revealed that Microsoft was pushing for a bigger share in the enterprise market with “professional-grade AGI.” He referred to this as an AI model that could do almost everything a human professional does. This would allow Microsoft to deliver powerful AI tools to its clients capable of performing routine tasks for knowledge workers.  advertisement  Suleyman predicted significant changes in the workforce were in store for the future. He reckoned that almost everyone who does their job on a computer could be at risk. The Microsoft AI boss explained,"White-collar jobs – those sitting in front of computers, whether lawyers, accountants, project managers, or marketers – most of these tasks will be fully automated by AI within the next 12 to 18 months."  The Microsoft AI chief’s comments come at a time when more companies are looking towards using AI. Anthropic’s Claude Cowork shook the stock markets a few days ago after the model threatened the future of SaaS companies such as Infosys and TCS.  Microsoft AI boss says making an AI model will be like making a podcast  As AI advances, Suleyman reckons, it will become easier for make new models, which could be curated to specific needs. He compared this to how one can easily write a blog or create a podcast. The Microsoft AI boss explained, "Creating a new model will be as simple as making a podcast or writing a blog. In the future, it will be possible to design AI tailored to the needs of every institution and individual on Earth."  Additionally, Suleyman added that within the next two to three years, AI agents will be able to become more efficient when it comes to handling the workflow of large institutions.  The Microsoft boss also hinted that the company was going to double down on its own AI models in the future, in a bid to reduce its reliance on OpenAI, following a new agreement between the two companies. He added, “We decided that this was a moment when we have to set about delivering on true AI self-sufficiency." Suleyman has teased that the new AI models from Microsoft may debut in 2026.  - Ends

title: Want higher writing scores in board exams? This is the secret
text: For many board aspirants, reading is often treated as a passive activity -- something to be completed quickly so that answers can be written faster. However, in the CBSE board exam framework, especially at the senior and secondary levels, reading is not merely about understanding “what” the text says, but about grasping “how” and “why” it says so.  Analytical reading trains students to engage with a text thoughtfully, observe patterns, interpret ideas, and evaluate the writer’s intent. This deeper engagement directly reflects in writing, whether in comprehension responses, analytical paragraphs, literature answers, or creative tasks.  advertisement  FROM READING SECTION TO WRITING EXCELLENCE  When students read a text analytically, they learn to decode the underlying meaning, identify the central concern of the writer, and recognise how characters, events, and literary devices work together to shape the message.  In short answers, this approach helps them respond directly to the question by making a clear analytical point, briefly justifying it with textual reference, and avoiding unnecessary narration.  In long answers, analytical reading allows students to structure responses thoughtfully—opening with an interpretative statement, developing arguments through analysis of character motivation, thematic depth, conflict, or symbolism, and concluding with the writer’s broader message or relevance.  To strengthen such answers, students can consciously use analytical phrases such as “This highlights the theme of,” “The writer subtly suggests,” “This contrast brings out,” “The character’s actions reflect,” “This moment serves as a turning point because,” and “Through this episode, the author critiques/emphasises.”  Phrases like “on a deeper level,” “this can be interpreted as,” “the underlying implication is,” and “the narrative technique reinforces” add clarity and depth to long answers, signalling critical engagement with the text.  ANALYTICAL READING AND LITERATURE ANSWERS  Literature is one of the strongest areas where analytical reading shows visible results. When students read prose, poetry, or drama analytically, they begin to connect themes, character motivations, and literary devices with the larger message of the text.  For instance, while reading a story that highlights human values, an analytical reader notes how incidents, dialogues, and settings contribute to the central theme.  Similarly, while studying a poem, attention to imagery, symbolism, and tone helps students move beyond paraphrasing to interpretation.  This approach enables them to write answers that are thoughtful, text-supported, and aligned with marking rubrics.  LEARNING FROM PRESCRIBED TEXTS  Several prescribed lessons across classes encourage analytical thinking. Stories that explore ethical dilemmas or poems that reflect social realities are designed to be read with sensitivity and depth.  When students analyse characters’ decisions, narrative shifts, or poetic contrasts, they gain language structures and expressions that can be effectively reused in their own writing.  advertisement  Such reading strengthens vocabulary, improves sentence construction, and enhances the ability to justify opinions—an essential requirement in long-answer questions.  BUILDING STRONG ANALYTICAL PARAGRAPHS  Analytical reading also helps students understand how strong paragraphs are built. By observing how authors introduce ideas, explain them logically, and support them with examples, students learn paragraph unity and coherence.  This is especially useful while attempting analytical paragraphs based on data, visuals, or short texts.  Students who read analytically are better prepared to interpret information, identify trends, and present conclusions clearly, which significantly improves scores in the writing section.  Readers who engage analytically naturally adopt a more discerning tone in their writing. They employ expressions such as “this underscores,” “this exemplifies,” “the implicit suggestion,” and “this reinforces the central argument.”  Such language signals critical engagement and elevates responses by aligning them with formal academic discourse.  AN EXAM-ORIENTED YET LIFELONG SKILL  From an educator’s perspective, analytical reading should not be seen as an additional burden but as a smart exam strategy. It reduces rote learning, sharpens interpretation skills, and improves time management during exams.  advertisement  More importantly, it empowers students to write answers that are relevant, structured, and expressive.  When students read with analysis, they automatically think like writers—and this thinking reflects in higher writing scores across sections.  READ TO WRITE BETTER  Ultimately, good writing in board exams is the result of good reading habits. Analytical reading bridges the gap between understanding and expression.  Students who consciously practise this skill not only score better but also develop confidence in handling unseen passages, analytical tasks, and literature questions.  Reading analytically today ensures writing effectively tomorrow -- a combination that leads to success not just in examinations, but in learning as a whole.  - Article by Sakshi, PGT, English, Manav Rachna International School, Charmwood  - Ends

title: Mahashivratri 2026 fasting during periods: Can you observe the fast?
text: Mahashivratri 2026 will be observed with devotion and night-long prayers across India and by Hindu communities worldwide. Fasting, or vrat, is considered an integral part of the celebration dedicated to Lord Shiva. However, one question resurfaces every year, can women observe Mahashivratri fast during menstruation? With evolving social norms, medical awareness and differing interpretations of tradition, it is important to separate belief from compulsion.  advertisement  Here’s what religious texts, customs and health experts suggest about fasting during periods and the broader spiritual meaning of Mahashivratri.  1. Can women fast on Mahashivratri 2026 during menstruation?  Traditionally, certain customs in some households advise women to avoid temple visits or ritual participation during menstruation. However, there is no universal scriptural ban across Hindu texts that explicitly forbids women from fasting or praying during their periods.  Many modern spiritual leaders and scholars emphasise that devotion is internal. The essence of Mahashivratri lies in meditation, self-discipline and remembrance of Lord Shiva, not merely physical rituals.  In contemporary practice, many women choose to observe the vrat during menstruation, especially if they feel physically comfortable. Others may modify the way they participate, such as praying at home instead of visiting temples.  Ultimately, the decision often depends on personal belief, family tradition and physical well-being.  2. Is fasting compulsory for observing Mahashivratri vrat?  Fasting on Mahashivratri is a widely followed tradition, but it is not universally compulsory.  Devotees observe different types of fasts:  Nirjala vrat (without food and water)  Phalahar vrat (fruits and milk)  Satvik meal once a day  Partial fasting or dietary restrictions  Religious scholars often stress that the spiritual intent matters more than the strictness of the fast. Chanting “Om Namah Shivaya,” performing Rudrabhishek, meditating and staying awake during jaagran are equally significant aspects of the festival.  If someone is unwell, menstruating, pregnant or dealing with health conditions, modifying the fast is generally considered acceptable.  3. What is the spiritual purpose of fasting on Mahashivratri?  Fasting during Mahashivratri symbolises purification of the body and mind. It is believed to:  Enhance self-discipline  Promote mental clarity  Reduce physical indulgence  Strengthen spiritual focus  According to tradition, Mahashivratri marks the divine union of Shiva and Parvati and represents the overcoming of darkness and ignorance. Devotees fast to cultivate detachment and devotion.  The night-long vigil signifies heightened awareness, a reminder to stay spiritually awake.  - Ends

title: Close to China border, India turns highway into runway for Rafales, Globemasters
text: Hardly a few hundred kilometres from the Line of Actual Control (LAC), India is set to operationalise its first highway airstrip in its Northeastern part. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to land on the 4.2 kilometre Emergency Landing Facility (ELF) stretch of a National Highway in Dibrugarh district of Assam on Saturday, February 14, marking its opening.  Around 16 Indian Air Force aircraft, including Rafales and Sukhois, will take part in a mega airshow. Several fighter jets are expected to land on the highway runway. The ELF stretch, part of the Dibrugarh-Moran National Highway, is in Upper Assam, not far from India's eastern frontier with China.  advertisement  Officials say it boosts national security and disaster preparedness. Geo intelligence expert Damien Symon on X said, "This airstrip enhances dispersed and survivable air power in crisis scenarios."  Days before its inauguration, videos circulating on social media showed IAF Rafale fighter jets and a C-17 Globemaster transport aircraft carrying out landings and touch-and-go operations on the highway strip.  Most of India's ELFs are situated in western, northern and central parts of the country. This is the first ELF in northeast India and close to the Chabua Air Force Station (AFS).  HIGHWAY TURNED INTO RUNWAY IN UPPER ASSAM, FIRST IN NORTHEAST  Unlocking another strategic potential, India has converted a portion of the Dibrugarh-Moran National Highway into an Emergency Landing Facility for the Indian Air Force.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi will land on the newly developed strip on Saturday, reported news agency PTI. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said, "The PM will be flying from New Delhi to Chabua Air Force base on Saturday morning. From there, he will take a flight and land at the Moran ELF in the district".  The 4.2-km stretch between Moran and Demow has been developed in coordination with the IAF.  These strips of highways allow fighter jets and heavy aircraft to land during emergencies or wartime contingencies. Such ELFs are designed to serve as alternate runways if airbases are targeted or rendered unusable. The Indian Air Force and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways have identified a total of 28 to 29 Emergency Landing Facilities (ELFs) to be developed across India. Approximately 15 facilities are reported as ready or active across various states.  Some of India's Emergency Landing Facilities are on the Taj Expressway, the Ganga Expressway, the NH-925A in Barmer (Rajasthan) and the Purvanchal Expressway (Uttar Pradesh).  This facility in Assam, the first in the Northeast, assumes added significance given its proximity to the Line of Actual Control with China. India has, in recent years, stepped up border infrastructure in the Northeast following tensions in eastern Ladakh.  Minister of Communications Jyotiraditya Scindia on X said that the blending of a highway and a runway reveal India's "strategic resolve".  "The Dibrugarh-Moran stretch of the National Highway in Assam can transform from a seamless road into an Emergency Landing Facility for India's frontline jets and transport," he wrote.  RAFALES, SUKHOIS, LIFTERS TO TAKE PART IN OPENING OF NORTHEAST'S FIRST HIGHWAY AIRSTRIP  advertisement  To mark the opening, the Indian Air Force will stage a large-scale airshow. Around 16 aircraft will either land on the strip or conduct fly-pasts within 30 minutes.  "Rafael, Sukhoi and other IAF aircraft will take part in the airshow, and many of the fighter jets will also land at the strip. This will be the first such elaborate exercise on an ELF," Himanta Biswa Sarma said.  While the Sarma mentioned Rafales and Sukhois, such ELFs are also built to handle heavy transport aircraft like the C-17 Globemaster and C-130J Super Hercules. These platforms are crucial for rapid troop deployment and logistics in border areas.  India has earlier operationalised similar highway landing strips in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. But this is the first such facility in the Northeast, a region that is strategically sensitive due to proximity with China, Bangladesh and Myanmar, and logistically challenging due to the terrain.  After landing at the ELF and witnessing the airshow, PM Modi will fly to Guwahati. There, he will inaugurate a new bridge over the Brahmaputra River. The Prime Minister would also inaugurate the temporary campus of IIM Guwahati and an AI-enabled hyperscale data centre. This would be PM Modi's third visit to Assam in three months. Assembly elections in Assam are likely in March-April.  Among all the projects, the ELF in Dibrugarh, the first highway-runway in the northeast, is crucial and will give India a strategic boost.  - Ends  Published By: Sushim Mukul Published On: Feb 12, 2026

title: No bail for Rajpal Yadav, court says he failed to honour commitment
text: Actor Rajpal Yadav will have to spend at least four more nights in the Tihar Jail after the Delhi High Court adjourned his bail hearing to Monday, February 16. The actor was pulled up by the court for reopening the case after failing to honour his commitment.  The court also issued a notice to Murli Projects Company, the company which gave a Rs 5 crore loan to Yadav in 2010 for his debut directorial, Ata Pata Lapataa, to file a response to the bail application. The matter pertains to nearly Rs 9 crore that Yadav allegedly failed to repay. During the hearing, Yadav's lawyers sought time from the court, stating that they needed instructions from him regarding the payment.  advertisement  The actor also told the court that Yadav needed to attend his niece's wedding in Shahjahanpur later this month. He has been in judicial custody at Tihar Jail since February 5.  Court pulls up Rajpal Yadav  During the proceedings, the Delhi High Court strongly reprimanded the actor. Justice Swarnakanta Sharma observed that Yadav's imprisonment was not because of the court's order but due to his own conduct. The court noted that Yadav had admitted to the liability multiple times.  "When you have already confessed to the offence, the question of suspending the sentence does not arise," the judge said.  "I don't understand what the argument is. The judge had said there were no merits to interfere with the conviction. You then said you would explore settlement, went to mediation and said you would pay. For years, you didn't make the payment. Now you want to reopen the case," the court said, asking the actor to explain the delay.  Justice Sharma further observed that Yadav had, on numerous occasions, acknowledged in court that he had taken the money and would repay it. He was sentenced to six months' imprisonment for failing to return the amount which accumulated to nearly Rs 9 crore over the years.  The court also noted that on at least two dozen occasions, Yadav had assured that he would clear the dues but did not fulfil the promise.  Meanwhile, after the matter reached court, several people from Bollywood and politics have reportedly announced financial assistance to help raise funds for the payment.  - Ends  Published By: Priya Pareek Published On: Feb 12, 2026

title: SL vs OMA: Sri Lanka set for Australia challenge after hammering Oman
text: Brief scores: Sri Lanka (225/5 in 20 ov) beat Oman (120/9 in 20 ov) by 105 runs in Pallekele in a Group B match.  SL vs OMA T20 WORLD CUP 2026: HIGHLIGHTS | SCORECARD  Sri Lanka continued their brilliant start to the T20 World Cup 2026 and got ready for their match against Australia with a 105-run win against Oman in Pallekele on Thursday, February 12. Fifties from Kusal Mendis and Pavan Rathnayake and a record-breaking half-century from captain Dasun Shanaka helped the hosts post a mammoth total of 225 runs in the first innings. In response, Oman were never even in the chase as regular wickets and mistakes meant that they could only get 120 runs in their 20 overs.  advertisement  The loss also meant that Oman are on the brink of an early exit from the competition, having lost their first match against Zimbabwe. The toss was won by Oman on a cloudy day in Pallekele and that was the only bit of excitement for Jatinder Singh and his Co. in the match.  Sri Lanka were dealt an early blow as Kamil Mishara was cleaned up in the second over. Mendis arrived and showed intent early with a couple of boundaries. Oman then had a moment of madness as they decided to take one of the worst reviews, much to the amusement of the commentators.  Nissanka and Mendis then piled on the runs before Jatinder redeemed himself for the earlier DRS howler with a smart call to send the Sri Lankan opener back to the pavilion. The score was 42 for two in 5.1 overs and Oman did have some belief to make something of the game. But the momentum was quickly shutdown by a Rathnayake storm that left Oman speechless.  RATHNAYAKE PUTS HIS HAND UP  "I played my normal game, so I enjoyed it. I played my normal game and I am very happy. Today we just finished it. From my point, we tried to give the boost and also in the end, we needed boundaries. We just followed it and stayed."  These were the words of Rathnayake after his whirlwind knock on Thursday, which played a big role in the win. There were questions about the quality of the Sri Lankan middle-order, but the 23-year-old answered with three boundaries out of the first four balls he faced.  With the experienced Mendis at the other end, the youngster continued to play with attacking intent and find boundaries when the opportunity presented itself. Mendis and Rathnayake played cautiously and ensured they got to 96 in 10 overs as Oman weren't disciplined with the ball.  Once both players understood that the threat from the Oman bowling was minimal, Rathnayake flexed his muscles and got to his maiden T20I fifty off just 24 balls and then he started to take apart the bowling. In an attempt to up the ante, Rathnayake fell, but his knock gives the co-hosts hope as they head to the business end. He ensured that a 94-run stand was set with Mendis and the momentum was on the co-hosts' side.  advertisement  Just when Oman thought they were clear of danger when Shanaka came in and continued the onslaught. The Sri Lankan captain was under some criticism for his own form after taking over from Charith Asalanka and he made a statement with the fastest fifty by a Sri Lankan player in T20Is.  Shanaka, aided by some wayward bowling from Oman, just sent the ball to all parts of the ground and got to his landmark in just 19 balls as Sri Lanka set themselves for a big finish.  While Shanaka and Mendis fell in quick succession, Wellalage and Kamindu Mendis put the finishing touches.  RUDE AWAKENING FOR OMAN  While Oman is one of the great stories in the T20 World Cup 2026, their performances have suggested that there is still a big gap in quality to give a tussle to the big names. The ongoing tournament has seen the associates cause headaches for the giants, but Oman never looked like they were even close to doing that in Pallekele.  They lost two wickets within the first two overs and from there, it was just Oman struggling to keep up with the required run-rate. Mohammad Nadeem and Wasim Ali provided some relief for Oman with their 42-run stand, but the moment the latter fell, the wheels just came off the run chase.  advertisement  Theekshana and Chameera picked up two wickets each but it was also some poor bit of running that cost Oman dearly. Vinayak Shukla and Sufyan Mehmood were run out and the overall intent seemed to be lacking.  While Nadeem got his fifty, a total of five boundaries and four sixes were hit in the entire Oman innings, which paints a pale picture as the hosts hit 22 boundaries and eight maximums. The games will come thick and fast for Oman, who will now face Ireland and Australia in their remaining fixtures.  For Sri Lanka, the next big challenge will be the one that can potentially decide one and two in Group B as they face the Aussies on February 16. title: Russia blocks WhatsApp over Meta non-compliance, pushes state-backed MAX messenger
text: Russia has fully blocked US-based messaging platform WhatsApp, owned by Meta Platforms, over what the Kremlin described as the company’s failure to comply with local laws. The move comes amid a broader push by Russian authorities to promote a state-backed “national messenger” called MAX.  Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the decision on Thursday, saying the government had implemented the block because of Meta’s non-compliance.  advertisement  "Due to Meta's unwillingness to comply with Russian law, such a decision was indeed made and implemented," Peskov told reporters, urging citizens to switch to MAX.  "MAX is an accessible alternative, a developing messenger, a national messenger, and it is available on the market for citizens as an alternative," he said.  Critics have described MAX as a surveillance tool, an allegation Russian authorities deny. Officials say the platform integrates various government-related services and aims to simplify citizens’ daily lives.  The move follows six months of mounting pressure on WhatsApp and reflects Moscow’s broader effort, particularly during wartime, to establish what it calls a “sovereign” communications infrastructure. Under this framework, foreign technology companies must comply with Russian laws or face removal from the market.  Meta Russia has already been designated as an extremist organisation. WhatsApp earlier complained that authorities were attempting to fully block its service.  "Today the Russian government attempted to fully block WhatsApp in an effort to drive people to a state-owned surveillance app," the company said in a statement.  "Trying to isolate over 100 million users from private and secure communication is a backwards step and can only lead to less safety for people in Russia".  Following the latest measures, some domain names associated with WhatsApp disappeared from Russia’s national register of domain names. As a result, devices inside Russia stopped receiving the app’s IP addresses, making access possible only through a virtual private network (VPN).  Roskomnadzor, Russia’s state communications regulator, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.  Authorities had already restricted WhatsApp and other messenger services in August, blocking users from completing phone calls on the platforms. Officials accused foreign-owned platforms of failing to share information with law enforcement in fraud and terrorism cases.  In December, Roskomnadzor said it was taking additional steps to gradually restrict WhatsApp. The regulator accused the app of continuing to violate Russian law and of being used "to organise and carry out terrorist acts on the territory of the country, to recruit their perpetrators and to commit fraud and other crimes."  Russian courts have repeatedly fined WhatsApp for failing to delete banned content. Authorities have also insisted that the company open a local representative office in Russia to comply with the law, which it has not done.  Since December, many Russians have relied on VPNs to access WhatsApp. Some users have shifted to rival messenger apps, though platforms such as Telegram are also facing pressure from authorities for similar reasons.  - Ends  With Reuters inputs. title: Russia bans WhatsApp because reasons, can India do it as well? It's complicated
text: There are several countries where WhatsApp is not allowed. On Thursday the list got a new name: Russia. The country, which has a tussle going on with the US and an active war with Ukraine, on Thursday banned WhatsApp. As the ban took place, both the Kremlin and whatsApp went to town with their own version of the story. Irrespective of who owns the truth in this battle of words, there is one country that must be closely looking at the fight. That country is India, because India has its own share of issues with WhatsApp.  advertisement  If Russia is banning WhatsApp, and countries like Iran have done it earlier, can India too push out WhatsApp? The answer is complicated. But before we explore that, let’s hear it from Russia and WhatsApp.  In a statement to the media, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said: “Due to Meta’s unwillingness to comply with Russian law, such a decision was indeed made and implemented.” While there is a bit of confusion around what Russia means by “unwillingness”, it is reportedly about storing local data locally. This is an issue on which even the Indian government has been rather pressing on tech companies like Meta and Google.  Russia has also said that if WhatsApp agrees to government demands, it would be allowed again. “This is a question of fulfilling the legislation. If the Meta fulfils this and enters into dialogue with Russian authorities, then we have the possibility of reaching an agreement,” Peskov reportedly said.  With no WhatsApp in the country, Russia is actively nudging and pushing people to use Max, a messenger app that is backed by the Russian government. “Max is an accessible alternative, a developing messenger, a national messenger, and it is available on the market for citizens as an alternative,” said Peskov.  WhatsApp's Russia story  Well, WhatsApp has a different story to tell. As the ban went into effect, Meta came out all guns blazing and accused Russia of censorship and of attempting to surveil its citizens. “Today the Russian government attempted to fully block WhatsApp in an effort to drive people to a state-owned surveillance app,” the company said in a statement posted on X. “Trying to isolate over 100 million users from private and secure communication is a backwards step and can only lead to less safety for people in Russia.”  Irrespective of who is right and who is wrong, the issue again highlights the matter of tech sovereignty, power of tech companies like WhatsApp, and what all a government can do to curb it. It also puts spotlight on the sporadic tussles that the Indian government and WhatsApp keep having from time to time. For example, just a week ago, WhatsApp had a rough moment in the Supreme Court over its privacy policy. So angry seemed the Supreme Court at the stance taken by WhatsApp that it threatened to ban the app in the country.  advertisement  The question then: can India also ban WhatsApp? The answer is complicated.  India is not Russia  If you are looking for a binary answer, it is quite simple: Yes, India can ban WhatsApp. After all, India is a sovereign country, just like Russia, and it can do what it wants when it comes to what it allows in the country and what it doesn’t. Example: TikTok. Banned in 2020, TikTok is still banned in the country and cannot be accessed.  But while both Russia and India are sovereign countries, their lived realities and the way they connect to the global system, which WhatsApp is a part of, are completely different. For a country like Russia and China, banning a service of a tech giant is much easier because of their dynamics with the US. In the case of India, dynamics are very different. If India moves to ban a tech giant, or its services, the US government is definitely going to get active and will pull whatever moves it can pull. For example, whenever the EU in recent years has made life difficult for the tech giants, the Trump administration has threatened Europeans with repercussions. India too will face similar threats if it moves against WhatsApp.  advertisement  Then there is the fact that when it comes to India, the tech giants themselves are more accommodating because they want to lose access to such a vast and hugely important market. For example, all big tech companies already comply with the Indian government demands on storing data locally. They are also, because India is not at overt or covert war with the US, willing to share user data with the Indian government when the demand is made through lawful procedures. The same companies do not extend the same courtesy and cooperation to Russian or Chinese governments. Not at the moment.  Finally, there is the scale of WhatsApp in India. In Russia around 100 million people use WhatsApp whereas in India the number is over 800 million. More significantly, for better or worse, WhatsApp has become a lifeline of digital lives in India. Businesses run on it, so do families. It is part of millions of communities and groups. A ban on WhatsApp would not only be disruptive to individual users but also to businesses. Given this reality a ban on WhatsApp, while possible, is going to be the last resort from the Indian government.  - Ends

title: Government clears procurement of 114 Rafale jets
text: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, has cleared the procurement of 114 Rafale fighter jets, marking a significant boost to the Indian Air Force's combat capabilities. This potential government-to-government (G2G) deal emphasises the 'Make in India' initiative, with plans for 40 to 50% indigenous content and the integration of Indian weapon systems.  The approval comes ahead of French President Emmanuel Macron's scheduled visit to India from February 17 to 19, signalling strong strategic trust between the two nations. In addition to the fighter jets, the DAC has also approved the procurement of six P-8I maritime surveillance aircraft. This move follows recent statements by the Vice Chief of Air Staff highlighting the Rafale as a key component for expanding the IAF's fighter jet arsenal. The deal is expected to involve significant technology transfer and domestic manufacturing, aligning with India's modernisation goals and strengthening its defence partnership with France.

title: Bengaluru man clings to speeding car's bonnet in shocking road rage video

title: Trump says he doesn't want to destroy PM's career. India reacts to viral video
text: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Thursday said it would take "appropriate action" after an old video of US President Donald Trump's remark on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's political career resurfaced on social media. Trump made the bizarre remark jokingly in October last year amid a strain in US-India ties over the trade deal and tariffs linked to Delhi's Russian oil purchases.  advertisement  A video of Trump's remark has emerged again on X, prompting reporters to question the MEA spokesperson during his weekly media briefing. Randhir Jaiswal, the MEA spokesperson, said he had not seen the video, but if it existed, "appropriate action" would be taken.  "I have not seen the video... However, if such a video exists, whether it is true or false, we will take appropriate action on it," Jaiswal said in tough remarks.  WHAT TRUMP SAID ON PM MODI'S CAREER?  The eccentric US President made the remarks on October 15, 2025, as he lavished praise on PM Modi after he claimed that India assured the US on halting oil purchases from Russia. Trump, being Trump, boasted even though India denied any such concrete assurance.  Speaking in the White House, Trump praised PM Modi as a "great man" and a time-tested leader. He then stressed that PM Modi "loves Trump".  The US President then took a second to gauge what he said and felt the need to offer a quick clarification. Trump quickly underlined that the word "love" should not be taken any differently, as he "doesn't want to destroy the political career" of PM Modi.  "Modi is a great man. He loves Trump... I don't want you to take the word love any differently. I don't want to destroy his political career," Trump chuckled in his own inimitable style.  The remarks, which a section of users portrayed as a threat to PM Modi from Trump, were, in essence, made in jest.  It came days after Trump wished PM Modi on his birthday on September 17, as India-US ties slowly came back on track. Cut back to February 2026, India and the US have now agreed to a trade deal, and ties are firmly on an upswing. Last week, Trump reduced tariffs on Indian goods to 18%, among the lowest in Asia, from a crippling 50%.  - Ends  Published By: Abhishek De Published On: Feb 12, 2026

title: Lamborghini crash case: Four days to arrest Shivam Mishra, bail in 6 hours
text: A Kanpur court on Thursday granted bail to a tobacco tycoon’s son, Shivam Mishra, hours after he was arrested for crashing his Lamborghini into pedestrians on Sunday. The 24-year-old Mishra, who argued his own case, was released on a personal bond of Rs 20,000, with the court citing 'no due legal process was followed' by the police in pursuing the matter.  advertisement  In the case related to the high-profile hit-and-run, the court rejected the police’s application for judicial remand of accused Shivam.  During the hearing, Shivam appeared in court and argued his own case, and the judge questioned aspects of the police investigation and the notices served.  According to the court’s ruling, the police did not properly follow the required procedure before arresting Mishra.  The judge observed that the notice that should have been issued under Section 35(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, was not served in accordance with the law.  The court also noted that the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court in the Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar case — which aim to prevent unnecessary arrests — were not adhered to.  Mishra was booked under relevant sections of the BNSS Act. The investigating officer had taken him into custody and requested a 14-day remand for further questioning.  However, after examining the case record and the manner in which the arrest was made, the court found procedural lapses and declined the remand request.  In its order, the court made it clear that an arrest carried out without following due process cannot be treated as valid. It went on to emphasise that legal safeguards must be respected during investigations.  The court directed that Mishra be released on a personal bond of 20,000, subject to certain conditions. He has been instructed to cooperate fully with the ongoing investigation, appear before the court as required, and refrain from influencing witnesses or tampering with evidence in any form.  The investigation in the case will continue in accordance with the law.  SHIVAM WAS ARRESTED HOURS AGO  Shivam Mishra was granted bail hours after he was arrested, days after a Lamborghini crash in Kanpur. Police maintained that he was driving the luxury car when it rammed into pedestrians and vehicles on VIP Road.  Authorities had sought his 14-day remand, stating he had been evading investigators and failing to cooperate.  DCP Atul Kumar Srivastava said five teams were formed after receiving inputs about Shivam’s whereabouts in the city.  advertisement  He was taken for a medical examination before being produced in court. Visuals showed him limping and being assisted by police personnel.  The accident occurred around 3 pm on Sunday when the speeding Lamborghini Revuelto, valued at over Rs 10 crore, lost control and struck people and vehicles before stopping on a divider. An FIR was lodged by injured e-rickshaw driver Mohd Taufeeq.  The case saw a twist when a man named Mohan claimed he was driving and alleged Shivam suffered a seizure.  However, police reports did not list Mohan as an accused, and the court declined to accept his surrender.  Officials cited CCTV footage, eyewitness statements, and videos suggesting Shivam was pulled from the driver’s seat after the crash. The car was seized for forensic analysis.  Previously, KK Mishra also claimed that Shivam was not behind the wheel of the car. Videos also went viral showing bouncers linked to the businessman trying to tear off the vehicle's registration plate, ostensibly to conceal the identity of its owner.  However, police told the court on Thursday that a thorough investigation had firmly established that Shivam was himself driving the Lamborghini at the time of the crash on Sunday night.  - Ends  Published By: Priya Pareek Published On: Feb 12, 2026

title: Bangladesh Election 2026 Live: Voting ends with 48% turnout, ballot counting begins
authors: New Delhi
text: Former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina has denounced the 2026 general elections as a "sham", accusing interim leader "killer-fascist" Muhammad Yunus of organising an illegal and unconstitutional vote without the participation of the Awami League.  In her statement, Hasina alleged that, "From the evening of 11 February, this farce began through the capture of polling centres, gunfire, the widespread use of money to buy votes, stamping ballot papers, and taking agents’ signatures on result sheets. From the morning of 12 February, voter turnout in most polling centres across the country was extremely low. Many polling stations in the capital and other parts of the country were completely empty of voters,"  She also argued mass boycott of the polls by citing the Election Commission’s briefing, which showed voter turnout until 11 a.m. (within three and a half hours) was only 14.96%. "This low participation at the peak voting period proves that the public boycotted and rejected this election without the Awami League," she alleged.  She added, "In this situation, we demand the cancellation of this voterless, illegal, and unconstitutional election; the resignation of Yunus; the withdrawal of false cases and the release of all political prisoners as well as teachers, journalists, intellectuals, and professionals; the removal of the suspension imposed on the activities of the Awami League; and the restoration of the people’s voting rights through the arrangement of a free, fair, and inclusive election under a neutral caretaker government." title: Nani's The Paradise exits March race, new release date announced
text: March 2026 was initially shaping up as a crowded window for major pan-India releases, with several big-budget films targeting the same period.
