Less than 6 months ago, they had defeated the same West Indian side 2-1 in a bilateral series. They need to believe that they can win 3 games in 4 meetings.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says stop learning coding, learn AI fluency instead
text: The next big skill may not be coding. It may just be asking better questions from AI.  In a January 2025 podcast with Cleo Abram, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that if he were a student today, he wouldn’t prioritise learning to code. He would prioritise learning how to interact with AI.  That single line has sparked a serious debate online after a video snippet from the podcast went viral on X.  advertisement  Huang’s point wasn’t that coding is useless. His argument was sharper. He said students should first learn how to “interact with ChatGPT” and other AI systems, and understand how to use them to become better lawyers, doctors, chemists, or engineers.  “Learning how to interact with AI is not unlike being someone who is really good at asking questions,” he said. Prompting, he added, requires “expertise in artistry”.  The point is that AI is not Google. And treating it like Google is a waste of both the sheer potential of AI, and of energy.  IS AI FLUENCY THE NEW DIVIDE?  The discussion under Huang’s podcast snippet on X turned into a great debate with views on the pros and cons of what the Nvidea CEO was suggesting.  One commenter summed it up in two words: AI fluency.  This is not just about using AI, or about typing a question and copying the answer. AI fluency is about knowing when to trust the output, when to push back, and how to break complex problems into smaller pieces the AI can handle.  It means iterating through conversations instead of expecting magic from a single prompt. It means combining your domain knowledge with AI’s pattern recognition.  That formula of domain expertise multiplied by AI fluency is how we can build our leverage today.  Without expertise, AI outputs are just noise. And without fluency, you’re barely scratching the surface.  If this becomes standard thinking, then in three years, the real divide in every industry may not be AI vs non-AI workers. It may be between people who know how to direct AI properly and those who don’t.  THE POWER OF THE ‘NEGATIVE PROMPT’  Another user pointed out something interesting: levelling up your AI fluency is not just telling AI what you want, but telling it what to avoid.  We need to avoid clichs, weak arguments, specific technical pitfalls, and oversimplification.  advertisement  This idea of building a ‘negative prompt’ in your head changes the quality of the output dramatically. It forces you to think critically before you even type.  And that is where Jensen Huang’s idea becomes clearer. AI prompting is not laziness. It can actually be a thinking exercise, but only if done properly.  The problem is, most people don’t use it that way.  They treat AI like a supercharged search engine. Type a question, get an answer, and move on. This approach underutilises the tool and increases dependence without deep understanding.  IS THIS DUMBING US DOWN?  Not everyone agrees with Huang about coding becoming irrelevant though.  One critic argued that coding is one of the most complex cognitive activities humans can engage in. It builds logic, abstraction, and structured thinking. Replacing that with “rhetoric” or prompt-writing may, in their words, be a “dumbing down” of humanity.  It’s a fair concern.  Coding trains the brain differently. It forces precision, and teaches you how systems actually work. If AI writes all the code and humans only describe what they want, are we losing something fundamental?  On the other hand, supporters argue that value is shifting from typing to thinking and verifying. AI agents will increasingly generate code. The human role will be to define problems clearly, evaluate outputs, and integrate them into real-world systems.  advertisement  We are watching this happen in real time now with the rise in vibe coding.  In that sense, the skill of AI fluency moves us up the ladder from focusing on execution to judgement.  WHAT ABOUT ERRORS AND TRUST?  Then comes the practical concern about using AI: how reliable is it?  One commenter asked an important question — would you pay for something that could be wrong 5% of the time?  Would a hospital trust an AI assistant that might misread blood reports? Would a company hire both a coder and an AI agent that sometimes produces buggy code? If every output needs double-checking, where is the return on investment?  This is not theoretical. AI still makes mistakes, and very confidently to boot.  And in high-stakes fields like medicine, law, finance, or aviation, even a small error rate is unacceptable.  That’s where domain expertise becomes non-negotiable. AI fluency without expertise is dangerous. You may not even know when the system is wrong.  advertisement  Which brings up another big worry.  IF NO ONE LEARNS DEEPLY, WHO BECOMES THE EXPERT?  If future generations focus only on asking AI the right questions, and not on mastering the underlying subjects, who becomes the expert 15 years from now?  If current experts stop teaching fundamentals and instead teach “how to ask AI”, are we slowly hollowing out expertise itself?  It’s a serious question. Because AI does not generate knowledge independently. It recombines patterns from existing knowledge created by humans.  If human expertise declines, what happens to the quality of AI systems over time?  However, we should note that Jensen Huang’s original comment did not suggest abandoning deep learning of subjects. In fact, he repeatedly framed AI as a tool to become a better doctor, better lawyer, better scientist. The expertise still comes first.  But online reactions show how easily the message can be misread.  advertisement  SO, IS THIS JUST ABOUT PROMPTING BETTER?  At first glance, what the Nvidia CEO is saying sounds like a fancy way of saying: learn to prompt better.  Ask clearer questions, add context, refine the output, tell the system what tone you want, tell it what to avoid -- that’s prompting, right?  Yes, but reducing the shift to “better prompts” misses the bigger picture.  Prompting is the visible skill, but AI fluency is the invisible one.  Anyone can learn prompt templates in an afternoon -- “Act as an expert”, “Break this into steps”, “Avoid clichs.” These tricks improve AI output quality quickly, but don’t automatically make someone good at using AI in a high-stakes profession.  The real difference shows up when domain expertise enters the room.  A law student asking AI to “write a strong argument” will get something polished. A seasoned lawyer, however, might say: draft a counter-argument, avoid relying on this precedent, stress-test the reasoning, identify logical gaps, and flag potential weaknesses a judge could question. That’s not just basic prompting; that’s an expert directing an AI tool.  Without domain knowledge, AI can sound impressive and still be subtly wrong. It can mix up numbers, misinterpret data, use an outdated case law, or overgeneralise research. And because the language is confident, the error is harder to detect.  That’s why AI fluency is not only about asking better questions. It’s also about knowing when to doubt the answers, and understanding that the first output is rarely the best one.  This involves breaking a complex problem into smaller parts, and setting boundaries (the “negative prompt” idea).  And most importantly, it means having enough subject knowledge to evaluate what comes back, because you cannot critique what you do not understand.  THE REAL QUESTION ISN’T REPLACEMENT  As the popular AI commentary says: “The question isn’t whether AI will replace you. It’s whether someone who knows how to use it better will.”  Two professionals with equal degrees may perform very differently today depending on how fluently they work with AI tools.  For students, this changes preparation strategies. It may not be coding versus no coding. It may be coding plus AI fluency. Or law plus AI fluency. Or medicine plus AI fluency.  Building a robust AI skill is not surrendering thinking to machines, but learning how to collaborate with them intelligently.  Right now, most people are still at the “Google search” stage.  If Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is right, the next competitive edge won’t belong to those who simply use AI. It will belong to those who know how to direct it — critically, creatively, and cautiously.  And that divide is already forming.  - Ends

title: Bride-to-be UP constable's 'abduction' turns out as elopement with murder accused
text: A suspected case of abduction turned out to be a love affair in Uttar Pradesh’s Meerut. On February 7, a 25-year-old female constable, working in the cybercrime cell in Aligarh, left her home ahead of her marriage ceremony. Suspecting a case of kidnapping, the family members filed a complaint against Ankit Chauhan, a murder accused, who was out on bail. However, as per the police, Chauhan and the female constable had a love affair, and hence the two eloped.  advertisement  The incident shocked the local inhabitants. According to sources, the woman was engaged to a local man and was supposed to get married on Sunday. However, on Saturday night, the woman suddenly went missing from her home. The event triggered suspicion among the family members, who then filed a complaint, accusing Chauhan of kidnapping charges.  Based on the complaint, the police soon began their search procedure by forming a team. From the beginning, the police suspected it was a case of a love affair, and the constable eloped with Chauhan of her own will. A senior police officer also confirmed their relationship to the press.  A day later, the police found the woman and took her to the local police station, where she recorded her statement. The woman then left with her parents.  Meanwhile, the police were also looking for Chauhan. Initially, they thought of apprehending him. However, Chauhan evaded the police and quietly surrendered at the district session court on Tuesday. The police surrounded the court earlier; however, he did not pose a threat.  - Ends  Published By: Akash Chatterjee Published On: Feb 12, 2026  Tune In

title: Jana Nayagan delay: How censor row led to pan-India hype for Vijay's film
text: When the release of Thalapathy Vijay's Jana Nayagan was postponed from its scheduled release date, January 9, at the eleventh hour due to censor certification issues, it seemed like a devastating setback for what was billed as the Tamil superstar's grand farewell to cinema. Yet, a month later, as the film navigates the revising committee route, an unexpected narrative has emerged: Could the delay actually be working in the film's favour?  advertisement  For the unaware, the makers of Jana Nayagan knocked on the doors of Madras High Court on January 6 after the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) withheld the certificate over an internal complaint. The film was locked in a legal standoff with the censor board for a month with multiple hearings and even a request from the Supreme Court. Since the litigation was taking a long time, the producer of Jana Nayagan decided to withdraw the case against CBFC on February 10, and proceed with the film's submission to the revising committee.  From a Tamil biggie to pan-India phenomenon  What was initially positioned as a Tamil blockbuster has now transformed into a pan-India talking point. The month-long legal battle between the film's producers, KVN Productions, and the CBFC, complete with High Court hearings, Supreme Court intervention, and now a revision committee review, has kept Jana Nayagan in the headlines far longer than a typical pre-release promotion ever could. Generally, the producers of Vijay's films do not spend much on marketing or promotions as a film starring the actor is promotion in itself. The pre-release songs and trailers are just enough to get the hype going.  Now, the curiosity factor has intensified exponentially. Instead of the usual two-week promotional blitz, Jana Nayagan has dominated social media and media across languages for over a month. From national media channels to regional trade publications, everyone is tracking the certification saga. This unprecedented coverage has given the film a reach way beyond the team intended to.  The numbers tell a story  Even amid uncertainty, Jana Nayagan crossed 1 million "I'm interested" markers on BookMyShow – approaching the 1.1 million recorded by Leo, which grossed over Rs 610 crore worldwide. Before the film was postponed, advance bookings peaked at over 4,50,000 tickets sold that later necessitated a refund – the largest single-day cancellation in Indian cinema history.  Vijay: A guaranteed star at the box office  The delay hasn't dampened commercial confidence, and for good reason. Vijay's track record speaks for itself: Leo (Rs 618.5 crore), The Greatest of All Time (Rs 460.3 crore), Varisu (303 crore), Bigil (Rs 321 crore) – every major release since 2018 has been a commercial success. His films have become events across India and overseas markets, with trade analysts noting that even his "average" performers recover costs comfortably thanks to strong pre-release business.  advertisement  Vijay is a guaranteed star at the box office. Theatre owners have benefitted from his films over the past years and always look forward to his movies as they bring in family audiences. In Tamil Nadu, when theatres see poor turnout, Vijay's films have often acted as a respite and kept many theatres afloat for the next few months.  Missing Pongal: A blessing or a curse?  Jana Nayagan was supposed to be released during the prime, 10-day Pongal holiday. Missing that window looked like a disaster at first, given that Pongal releases usually have long runs, especially with families. But the delay might have actually worked in the film's favour, generating some buzz about its content.  Every court hearing, every revising committee update, every speculation about release dates has kept fans engaged and invested in ways standard promotional campaigns rarely achieve.  The international theatre challenge  However, not everything is in favour of the film. Theater chains in North America and the UK expressed dissatisfaction after the Jana Nayagan was postponed. Securing the same screen count for a rescheduled release could prove challenging with Hollywood releases like Wuthering Heights, Predator: Badlands, and Scream 7 set to take up screen space. However, the absence of major titles in late February provides an opportunity if certification comes through quickly.  advertisement  The election wildcard  The biggest risk factor for the film isn't the censor board or international theatres, but it could be the Election Commission of India (ECI). With Tamil Nadu Assembly elections expected to be announced by the end of February or early March, the ECI has authority to halt a film's screening if it believes the content could influence voters. Given that Vijay is contesting as leader of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and Jana Nayagan reportedly has rousing political speeches, this poses a genuine threat for release.  Is the delay a blessing?  Partially, yes. It has generated unprecedented buzz, transformed a regional film into a pan-India phenomenon, and kept Vijay's farewell film in constant conversation. But, there are also minimal risk factors discussed above.  For now, the entire industry watches and waits. When Jana Nayagan finally releases, it won't just be a farewell to Thalapathy Vijay the actor – it will be the culmination of one of the major delays in Tamil Cinema.  - Ends

title: I will be the kingmaker: Humayun Kabir vows to back BJP over TMC in Bengal
text: Humayun Kabir, founder of the newly formed Janta Unnayan Party (JUP), has declared that he intends to play "kingmaker" in the upcoming West Bengal Assembly elections and is prepared to back the BJP if it helps keep the Trinamool Congress (TMC) out of power.  Kabir launched his party after being expelled from the Trinamool amid a major controversy over his vow to construct a Babri Masjid in Murshidabad’s Beldanga.  advertisement  Now positioning himself as a decisive post-poll player, Kabir said his primary objective is to remove the ruling Trinamool government, even if it requires unconventional alliances.  "I will be a kingmaker. I will make a government," Kabir asserted, predicting a fractured mandate in the state.  He said the next Assembly election is likely to produce a hung verdict. "If there is a 'tishanku (hung Assembly)' situation, someone has to form a government. The government should be formed," he said.  Clarifying his stand on possible alliances, Kabir maintained that he would not formally invite the BJP but is open to outside support arrangements.  "If they give me support to stop TMC, I will support them from outside. If they support me from outside, I will not join them. I will not join TMC. I will join BJP," he said, underlining his flexibility in negotiations.  At the same time, he did not rule out accepting support from Trinamool if circumstances demanded.  Kabir also hinted at broader electoral calculations, claiming he is ready to contest a large number of seats and engage in seat-sharing discussions.  He revealed that the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) of Asaduddin Owaisi may contest around 15 seats in Bengal, adding that talks are ongoing.  "They asked for 15 seats. I thought if I give 10 or 12, they may agree," he said, noting that he plans to meet the AIMIM chief after Ramadan.  Kabir predicted that the current ruling party would slip in rankings. "The power that is in power will be pushed to the third position. I will take the first position," he claimed, while suggesting that the BJP is attempting to expand its seat tally significantly.  22-KM-LONG MARCH FOR BABRI MASJID  His recent 22-kilometre march in support of constructing a Babri Masjid in Beldanga has kept him at the centre of political debate.  Kabir said he had been announcing the mosque project for two months and maintained that it was not unconstitutional.  "There was a court. The High Court assumed that there was no objection to the construction," he said, adding that public participation in the march was overwhelming. "When I went to start my work, there were lakhs of people," he claimed.  advertisement  The mosque initiative has drawn sharp criticism from the BJP, with party leaders alleging that the move is politically motivated.  Trinamool leaders, meanwhile, have distanced themselves from Kabir ever since his suspension.  On the Vande Mataram controversy, Kabir adopted a conciliatory tone.  "The slogan of Vande Mataram of India does not need to be opposed. The flag of India should be respected," he said, adding that patriotism should not be contentious.  With his new party and assertive posturing, Kabir has signalled that he intends to be a pivotal figure in Bengal’s evolving political landscape.  - Ends  Published By: Vivek Published On: Feb 12, 2026

title: A 90-year-old man was sold a 100-year insurance policy. Why blaming the bank is not enough
text: A 90-year-old man was sold a life insurance policy that will mature in 2124.  Read that again.  A man born before Independence was signed up for a financial product stretching into the next century. The annual premium was Rs 2 lakh. Two installments were reportedly debited before the family realised what had happened.  This was not satire. It was not a clerical typo. It was a policy processed, documented, and issued.  advertisement  The case was highlighted on social media by Saketh R, who said the elderly customer, Venkatachalam V Iyer, is his wife’s grandfather and has been banking with the same Canara Bank branch for several decades.  After the matter gained traction online, Saketh later posted an update saying the money had been credited back to the account and that he had deleted his earlier tweet. He thanked Canara Bank staff for what he described as a quick resolution and also thanked those who supported the issue online.  The refund brought immediate relief to the family, but it also raised a harder question. Would the money have been returned if the case had not gone viral?  Because mis-selling in India is not a one-branch problem. It is a structural vulnerability.  MIS-SELLING COMPLAINTS ON THE RISE  According to the latest figures from the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) through its Bima Bharosa grievance system, more than 2.5 lakh insurance grievances were recorded in FY2024-25. Roughly 1.2 lakh of these related to life insurance.  Complaints categorised under unfair business practices, which include mis-selling and improper disclosure, account for over one-fifth of life insurance grievances and have risen year-on-year.  That means tens of thousands of policyholders each year formally allege that what they were sold did not match what they were told.  This is the ecosystem within which the 90-year-old’s case sits.  India Today.in has been actively pursuing stories on mis-selling, highlighting how unsuitable insurance products are often pushed as safe investments and how systemic gaps in oversight allow such cases to repeat.  On the banking side, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has flagged concerns around improper sale of third-party products. The central bank has also proposed draft guidelines aimed at tightening how banks sell financial products, including insurance.  The framework emphasised suitability, explicit consent and compensation in cases of proven mis-selling. It also contemplates supervisory action and penalties.  The move is welcome. But it remains a proposal.  WHY SENIOR CITIZENS NEED URGENT PROTECTION  Selling a long-tenure, high-premium policy to a 90-year-old raises obvious suitability questions. But the vulnerability is not about age alone. It is about structure.  advertisement  IndiaToday.in had highlighted this in an earlier report.  Shilpa Arora, co-founder and COO at Insurance Samadhan, said the system must automatically identify certain sales as high risk. “Any life insurance proposal where the proposer is above 60 and the life insured is someone else should automatically be treated as a red-flag case,” she added.  “There is inherent vulnerability in that structure. Safeguards must activate before issuance, not after a complaint arises.”  According to Arora, enhanced scrutiny should not depend on social media attention.  “Suitability cannot remain a tick-box formality,” she said. “There must be a mandatory-recorded suitability conversation in such cases.”  She recommended a structured video or audio interaction conducted in the presence of a neutral, insurer-appointed but regulator-mandated verifier.  During that interaction, the product type must be clearly explained. Lock-in periods and surrender penalties must be disclosed. The risk versus return profile must be clarified. It must be explicitly stated whether the policy is insurance or investment.  “The recording should be stored and auditable,” she said. “If a dispute arises later, there should be clear evidence of what was explained.”  advertisement  In cases where the proposer and life insured are different individuals, she believes another layer is critical.  “There must be a separate confirmation call directly with the life insured,” Arora said. “Product details, tenure, premium obligation and beneficiary structure should be explained independently. Consent should be recorded separately. This prevents situations where the insured later claims lack of awareness or misrepresentation.”  Simply put, Arora, like many other experts, believes prevention must be built into the process, not triggered by public outrage.  THE INCENTIVE STRUCTURE QUESTION  Blaming the bank feels instinctive. The sale happened at a branch counter. But mis-selling often reflects incentive architecture rather than isolated misconduct.  Banks earn commissions from distributing insurance. Branch staff operate under cross-sell targets. Insurers depend heavily on bancassurance channels for premium growth. Quarterly performance metrics reward volume.  In such an environment, suitability can quietly lose ground to sales numbers.  If a policy was processed and issued, it also passed documentation and underwriting checks. That widens the circle of accountability.  Were entry-age norms strictly applied? Was suitability meaningfully assessed or merely documented? Was consent explained in substance or obtained in form?  These are systemic questions.  RBI'S PROPOSAL WELCOME, BUT NOT ENOUGH  The RBI has signalled that it recognises mis-selling as more than an isolated misconduct issue. Its draft guidelines propose clearer suitability norms, stronger disclosure requirements and the possibility of penalties and supervisory action against banks found guilty of mis-selling third-party products.  advertisement  That shift in tone matters.  For years, accountability in bancassurance has been diffused between distributors and insurers. A framework that explicitly places responsibility on banks could alter internal controls and compliance behaviour.  But the guidelines are still in draft form.  The real test will lie in how firmly they are implemented once finalised.  Will penalties be meaningful enough to change incentive structures at the branch level? Will repeat violations trigger escalating supervisory scrutiny rather than routine warnings? Will enforcement actions be made public to create deterrence across the sector? And will vulnerable categories such as senior citizens receive specific procedural safeguards?  Regulatory intent is important. Enforcement consistency is decisive. Until there is visible follow-through, mis-selling risks remain a recurring headline rather than a solved problem.  SCALE OF INDIA'S MIS-SELLING MENACE  In this case, the money was returned. The tweets were deleted. The branch acted swiftly once the spotlight turned on. That is good.  But the larger concern remains. A 90-year-old who had banked with the same branch for decades should not have required social media traction to secure a review.  advertisement  A policy maturing in 2124 may sound bizarre. The system that processed it is not bizarre. It is structured around distribution incentives and procedural compliance.  Blaming the bank alone may satisfy immediate anger. Fixing mis-selling requires regulators, insurers and banks to realign incentives, embed safeguards and ensure that suitability is real, not merely recorded.  The refund closes this case. It does not close the question.  - Ends

title: Sham election by killer Yunus: Sheikh Hasina seeks cancellation of Bangladesh polls
text: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has demanded the cancellation of the country’s latest national election, describing it as a “sham election staged by the killer, fascist Muhammad Yunus” and calling for his resignation.  In a statement issued in response to the polls, Hasina demanded “the cancellation of this voterless, illegal, and unconstitutional election; the resignation of Yunus; the withdrawal of false cases and the release of all political prisoners as well as teachers, journalists, intellectuals, and professionals; the removal of the suspension imposed on the activities of the Awami League; and the restoration of the people’s voting rights through the arrangement of a free, fair, and inclusive election under a neutral caretaker government.”  advertisement  In her statement, Hasina thanked “the masses at all levels, including mothers, sisters, and minority communities” for rejecting what she termed a fraudulent exercise organised by Yunus, whom she accused of seizing power “illegally and unconstitutionally.”  Tap here for the Bangladesh polls live updates  “Today’s so-called election organised by Yunus, who took power through illegal and unconstitutional means, was essentially a carefully planned farce,” Hasina said. She alleged that the election disregarded “the people’s voting rights, democratic values, and the spirit of the constitution” and was arranged “without the Awami League and without voters.”  Hasina claimed that irregularities began on the evening of 11 February, alleging the capture of polling centres, gunfire, the widespread use of money to buy votes, stamping of ballot papers, and the taking of agents’ signatures on result sheets. She further alleged that from the morning of 12 February, voter turnout in most polling centres across the country remained extremely low, with many polling stations in the capital and other parts of the country “completely empty of voters.”  Citing the Election Commission’s briefing, she said voter turnout until 11 am, within three and a half hours of voting, stood at 14.96%. “This low participation at the peak voting period proves that the public boycotted and rejected this election without the Awami League,” she said.  Hasina also alleged that, in recent days, Awami League voters, supporters, well-wishers and minority communities faced “continuous attacks, arrests, intimidation, and an atmosphere of fear” in an attempt to forcibly take them to polling stations. Despite this, she said, they “boycotted and rejected this fraudulent election,” resulting in most polling centres being “effectively without voters.”  She further questioned the integrity of the voter list, claiming that “the number of voters on the voter list, especially in Dhaka, has increased abnormally, which is highly questionable and unbelievable.”  - Ends  Published By: Priya Pareek Published On: Feb 12, 2026

title: Elon Musk wants to launch spacecraft from Moon to hunt for aliens. Here's his plan
text: Elon Musk has sparked fresh excitement about our future in space, sharing bold plans for the Moon that mix advanced technology with big questions about life in the universe.  In a recent update on X, the SpaceX founder described Moonbase Alpha as the heart of a system that uses powerful launchers to send AI satellites deep into space, while creating a self-sustaining city on the Moon and hunting for signs of ancient alien civilisations.  advertisement  WHAT IS A MASS DRIVER, AND WHY BUILD ONE ON THE MOON?  A mass driver is a long electromagnetic track that accelerates objects to high speeds, like a super-powered catapult.  On the Moon, with its weak gravity and no air resistance, it could fling AI satellites into deep space one after another with a satisfying "shoom, shoom" sound, as Musk puts it.  This method saves huge amounts of fuel compared to launching from Earth. Satellites built with Moon-made solar panels and parts could carry massive computing power for AI, potentially reaching thousands of gigawatts worth each year.  HOW WILL MOONBASE ALPHA BECOME A SELF-SUSTAINING CITY?  The base would start small but grow into a real city where people live independently.  It would use solar power from constant sunlight, pull water from ice at the poles for fuel, and recycle everything in closed systems. Artistic view of AI probes venturing into deep space for potential discoveries. (Photo: Generative AI/Radifah Kabir/India Today)  Factories there would build those heavy AI satellites, feeding the mass driver for launches.  Musk sees this lunar city as a key step toward settling Mars and making humanity multi-planetary.  WHY DOES MUSK WANT TO SEARCH FOR ANCIENT ALIEN CIVILISATIONS?  Musk's vision goes beyond tech to wonder: are we alone?  By sending AI probes deep into space, we might spot ruins, signals, or leftovers from civilisations that thrived for millions of years.  He believes exploring far and wide could reveal if others existed before us, changing everything we know about the universe. Concept art showing Moonbase Alpha as an expanding lunar settlement with Starship support. (Photo: Generative AI/Radifah Kabir/India Today)  This drive pushes the whole Moon plan forward.  With Starship rockets advancing fast, these ideas are moving from dreams to possible reality.  The Moon could soon serve as our launchpad to the stars and maybe even answers to life's biggest mysteries.  - Ends  Published By: Radifah Kabir Published On: Feb 12, 2026  Tune In

title: Vijaya Ekadashi 2026: Offer these things to Lord Vishnu for success, prosperity
text: Vijaya Ekadashi 2026 is one of the most spiritually significant Ekadashis dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Observed during the Krishna Paksha of Phalguna month, this sacred day is believed to remove obstacles, grant victory in difficult situations and bring prosperity into one’s life. The word “Vijaya” itself means victory, and scriptures describe this Ekadashi as especially powerful for overcoming hardships and fulfilling heartfelt wishes. Devotees observe fasting, perform Vishnu puja and offer sacred items believed to invoke divine blessings for success, peace and spiritual upliftment.  advertisement  1. What is the significance of Vijaya Ekadashi 2026 in hindu tradition?  According to Hindu scriptures, Vijaya Ekadashi holds immense spiritual merit. It is believed that Lord Rama observed this Ekadashi before crossing the ocean to Lanka, seeking divine blessings for victory.  The day symbolises faith, discipline and surrender to Lord Vishnu. Devotees believe observing this fast:  Removes obstacles in career and personal life  Brings success in important endeavours  Cleanses past karmas  Grants spiritual strength  Vijaya Ekadashi is considered particularly auspicious for those seeking stability, progress and divine guidance.  2. Which Offerings Should Be Made to Lord Vishnu on This Sacred Day?  On Vijaya Ekadashi 2026, devotees traditionally offer specific items to please Lord Vishnu:  Tulsi leaves  Yellow flowers  Chandan (sandalwood paste)  Panchamrit  Fruits and satvik sweets  Incense and ghee diya  Offering these items with devotion is believed to amplify the spiritual benefits of the fast.  Yellow-coloured foods and garments are also considered auspicious, as yellow is associated with Lord Vishnu and prosperity.  3. How do tulsi leaves, chandan and panchamrit play a role in the puja?  Tulsi leaves hold special significance in Vishnu worship. It is believed that offering Tulsi with sincerity pleases Lord Vishnu instantly. No Vishnu puja is considered complete without Tulsi.  Chandan (sandalwood paste) symbolises purity and calmness. Applying chandan to the idol or image of Lord Vishnu represents devotion and respect.  Panchamrit — a sacred mixture of milk, curd, honey, sugar and ghee, is used for ritual bathing (abhishek). It signifies nourishment, sweetness and abundance.  Together, these offerings are believed to invite divine blessings and remove negativity from life.  - Ends

title: US tweaks to trade deal factsheet reflect shared understanding, says government
text: The government on Thursday said recent changes made by the United States to its trade deal factsheet reflect the shared understanding reached between the two countries earlier this month on a framework for an interim trade agreement.  The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) underlined that the India-US Joint Statement issued on 7 February 2026 remains the basis of the agreement, and both sides will now work towards implementing this framework and finalising the Interim Agreement. “The Joint Statement is the framework and remains the basis of our mutual understanding in the matter,” the MEA said.  advertisement  WHITE HOUSE EDITS FACT SHEET AFTER RELEASE  A day after the White House released its factsheet outlining key elements of the interim trade deal, the document was quietly revised to reflect agreed positions more accurately. The original version had stated that India “commits” to buying more than USD 500 billion worth of US goods, including energy, technology and other products, over a defined period. That wording was softened in the updated factsheet to say India “intends” to buy such goods, aligning the language with the joint statement agreed by both sides.  The revisions also removed references to “certain pulses” from the list of US agricultural products on which India would reduce or eliminate tariffs, a change seen as sensitive given the importance of the sector domestically.  CHANGES TO DIGITAL TRADE AND TARIFFS  In addition, the earlier version’s language about India “removing its digital services taxes” was dropped from the revised factsheet. The updated version instead states that India has committed to negotiating bilateral digital trade rules – a shift suggesting that some terms are still under discussion.  On tariffs, the framework envisages reciprocal cuts: the US has agreed to lower tariffs on Indian goods to around 18 per cent from previous higher levels, while India will reduce or eliminate import duties on US industrial products and a broad range of American food and agricultural items (minus the now-omitted pulses).  FRAMEWORK TO FINAL AGREEMENT  The MEA reiterated that the February 7 joint statement, which laid out the framework for a reciprocal and mutually beneficial trade agreement, continues to guide both sides. The revised factsheet amendments, New Delhi says, reflect the mutual understandings contained in that statement and will feed into negotiations on the interim pact.  Officials on both sides aim to finalise the trade deal by mid-March 2026, with implementation of tariff cuts and related provisions expected to follow thereafter.  - Ends  Published By: Priya Pareek Published On: Feb 12, 2026

title: India to get 114 Rafale jets as government clears Rs 3.25 lakh crore deal: Sources
text: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), led by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, on Thursday approved the procurement of 114 Rafale fighter jets, a move set to significantly enhance the Indian Air Force's operational capability, defence sources close to the development told India Today TV. The clearance of the mega Rs 3.25 lakh crore deal came ahead of French President Emmanuel Macron's visit later this month.  advertisement  Sources said that the DAC granted the Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) for the multi-billion-dollar programme. The Defence Procurement Board, chaired by the Defence Secretary, had already cleared the Rafale acquisition proposal last month, bringing formal negotiations with Dassault Aviation closer to conclusion.  Valued at roughly Rs 3.25 lakh crore, the deal is among India's largest fighter aircraft procurements. The announcement came as the IAF is grappling with an acute squadron shortfall, operating around 29 fighter squadrons against a sanctioned strength of 42 amid rising threat perceptions along India's western and northern borders.  Rafale jets are manufactured by French defence major Dassault Aviation.  Under the plan, 18 jets will be delivered in fly-away condition, while the remaining 96 will be assembled in India. Around 80 per cent of the fleet is projected to be manufactured domestically, with indigenous content potentially reaching 60 per cent under the Make in India initiative.  The IAF will induct 88 single-seat and 26 twin-seat variants, sources said. Dassault Aviation is likely to partner with Indian private sector companies for local manufacturing, assembly, and support, strengthening India's domestic defence production ecosystem.  The Air Force received its first five Rafale jets at Air Force Station Ambala in July 2020, later formally inducting them. Currently, India operates two Rafale squadrons: No. 17 "Golden Arrows" in Ambala, Haryana, and No. 101 'Falcons' in West Bengal's Hasimara, with the latter officially commissioned in July 2021.  - Ends  Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Feb 12, 2026  Tune In

title: Boycott 2.0? Afghanistan players withdraw from PSL auction after Pakistan's backlash
text: In what is now yet another major controversy to rock cricket in South Asia in recent months, Afghanistan players have pulled out of the Pakistan Super League's inaugural player auction—a troubling pattern that suggests geopolitical tensions are increasingly dictating the region's cricketing landscape.  Top Afghan cricketers, including Mujeeb ur Rehman, Seddiqullah Atal, Mohammad Nabi, Waqar Salamkheil, and Fazalhaq Farooqi, had initially registered for Wednesday's auction in Lahore. Still, they withdrew their names ahead of the proceedings, according to a franchise owner.  advertisement  ECHOES OF MUSTAFIZUR CONTROVERSY  The mass withdrawal follows strikingly similar controversies that have plagued the region's premier T20 leagues. Just weeks ago, the BCCI instructed Kolkata Knight Riders to release Bangladesh pacer Mustafizur Rahman despite his Rs 9.20 crore signing at the December 2025 mini-auction, succumbing to intense political backlash and pressure from religious groups over the safety of minorities in Bangladesh.  Now, it's Pakistan's turn to witness cricket becoming collateral damage in diplomatic disputes—and the coincidence is impossible to ignore.  GURBAZ'S BACKLASH TRIGGERS MASS WITHDRAWAL  The Afghan players' withdrawal came after widespread backlash over Peshawar Zalmi's direct signing of Afghanistan opener Rahmanullah Gurbaz, who subsequently pulled out of the PSL amid the controversy—a sequence eerily reminiscent of the Mustafizur saga.  PSL CEO Salman Naseer offered conflicting accounts of what transpired. While claiming that some Afghanistan players were listed in the auction pool, but no franchise selected them, he acknowledged the undeniable political reality at play.  "There was severe backlash after Zalmi signed Gurbaz because of the fractured relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan, and after Gurbaz pulled himself out of the PSL. So, the other players also decided it was better to avoid backlash," Naseer explained as quoted by PTI.  PATTERN OF POLITICAL INTERFERENCE  The parallels across all three controversies are hard to ignore. Just as the BCCI cited "recent developments" when instructing KKR to release Mustafizur, the PSL is now grappling with its own geopolitical crisis affecting player participation.  Relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been deeply strained since late last year when Pakistan's military conducted aerial strikes in selected areas of Afghanistan, claiming to target militant hideouts. The military action sparked angry responses from several Afghan cricketers on social media, triggering heated exchanges with Pakistani accounts.  Several Afghanistan players had publicly criticised the Pakistan government on social media, receiving reciprocal responses from Pakistani handles—much like the charged atmosphere that surrounded Mustafizur's release from the IPL amid concerns over minority safety in Bangladesh.  CRICKET CAUGHT IN DIPLOMATIC CROSSFIRE  The fact that three major cricketing nations in South Asia have faced politically-motivated boycott controversies within a matter of weeks underscores a disturbing trend: cricket—once celebrated as a unifying force in the region—is increasingly becoming a casualty of deteriorating diplomatic relations.  For cricket administrators and fans alike, the question looms larger than ever: is this the new normal for cricket, where political winds determine who plays and who doesn't?  - Ends

title: Aamir reacts to SRK-Salman's viral Pathaan scene: Nobody is indispensable
text: Actor Aamir Khan reacted to Shah Rukh Khan and Salman Khan's viral clip from director Siddharth Anand's Pathaan. It's a part of the post-credits scene from the film, where Salman's Tiger and Shah Rukh's Pathaan are heard talking about how they are irreplaceable. Aamir reflected on the scene and addressed the conversation around the "Khans" being the last of the stars.  advertisement  The actor, in an interview with Variety, said, "You know, there was a very funny scene in Pathaan. I don't even know whether I should mention this, but I haven't watched the movie because I don't watch that many films. But I was told about the scene and I saw it on YouTube. Salman and Shah Rukh are sitting at the end of the film and discussing who is going to... It was tongue-in-cheek. It was about the film, but it was also about outside the film. Usme masti, mazaak tha (That was all for the sake of fun and jokes)... and people laughed as well."  "Without taking names, a lot of people guessed what they were trying to say. But today, those same young actors have shown us that not only are they there, they can give us a run for our money - Chhaava with Vicky Kaushal, Animal with Ranbir Kapoor, Dhurandhar with Ranveer. They're there. They're very capable of taking over from us. I would say they are very talented actors, perhaps more talented than us. They are staking a claim for a rightful place. So they have answered without saying anything; they've answered with their work. Which is fantastic. I really appreciate that. It's wonderful to see that," he added.  Aamir also emphasised how people have been saying that the "time of superstars is gone." "According to me, every generation and every period will have its own heroes or heroines. Irrespective of gender, there will be people who touch people's hearts in a way that connects widely. A lot of people have been saying that the time of superstars is gone – these are the last of the Mohicans. But aisa kuch nahi hai (It's nothing like that). Yeh sab hum logon ko dil behlaane ke liye... naya generation naya superstar layega (It's all meant to please us...new generation will bring new superstars)," the 60-year-old added.  "And you have new stars being thrown up. Saiyaara is a huge hit. Chunky's nephew is in the film. He's a young, talented actor who's come up. It will keep happening. I don't think it's something of the past. Nobody's indispensable in this world. There will always be people who are better than you, more hardworking than you, more talented than you, who will come in and take your place. That is the cycle of life, as The Lion King teaches us. It's okay, and you should welcome stars. Hum log bhi lifelong nahi rahenge (We won't be around for too long)," Aamir concluded.  advertisement  Aamir's next production, Ek Din, is set to release on May 1, 2026. The romantic-drama features actors Junaid Khan and Sai Pallavi in pivotal characters.  Aamir is also backing director Rajkumar Santoshi's Lahore 1947, featuring Sunny Deol, Preity Zinta and Karan Deol in key roles.  - Ends  Published By: Anurag Bohra Published On: Feb 12, 2026

title: Kanpur Lamborghini crash: Shivam Mishra granted bail hours after arrest
text: A court in Kanpur has released Shivam Mishra on a personal bond of 20,000 rupees following his arrest in the high-profile Lamborghini crash case that left six people injured. Despite CCTV footage appearing to show Mishra behind the wheel, the court rejected the police's application for judicial remand, citing a lack of concrete evidence and lapses in the initial investigation. The proceedings revealed that Mishra's family had allegedly attempted to float a 'ghost driver' theory to shield him, and no medical test for alcohol was conducted within the mandatory 24-hour window. While the court directed Mishra to cooperate with the ongoing probe, the police have expressed intentions to file a charge sheet and investigate the filing of false affidavits by the family. The case has sparked significant public outcry over alleged police negligence and the perceived ease with which influential individuals can evade the law through 'money and muscle power'.

title: Sooraj Barjatya's Sangamarmar teaser out; Sourabh Raaj Jain, Sheen Dass lead cast

title: Imran Khan lost 85% vision in right eye? Pak Supreme Court orders medical review
text: Pakistan’s Supreme Court on Thursday ordered an urgent medical evaluation of former Prime Minister Imran Khan after a report said he has lost 85% of vision in his right eye. Barrister Salman Safdar, appointed as amicus curiae, submitted a detailed report to the court after meeting Khan at Rawalpindi’s Adiala Jail. The report states that Khan currently retains only 15% vision in his right eye.  advertisement  A two-member bench comprising Chief Justice Yahya Afridi and Justice Shahid Bilal Hasan heard the matter. After reviewing the findings, the court directed the government to conduct a comprehensive medical examination, including a specialist ophthalmological review, before February 16.  The bench also instructed authorities to facilitate telephone contact between Khan and his sons, Qasim and Sulaiman, and allow access to his personal physicians.  MEDICAL FINDINGS PLACED BEFORE COURT  According to the report submitted by the amicus curiae, Khan had normal 6/6 vision in both eyes as recently as October 2025. He later began experiencing persistent blurred and hazy vision and allegedly raised repeated complaints with jail authorities.  The report states that Khan subsequently suffered a sudden and complete loss of vision in his right eye. An ophthalmologist at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) Hospital diagnosed a blood clot that caused severe damage. Despite treatment, including an injection, only 15% vision reportedly remains in the affected eye.  While the court declined a request to reassess a medical procedure conducted on January 24 at PIMS Hospital, Chief Justice Afridi observed that the health of a prisoner is the responsibility of the state and must be protected.  EMOTIONAL SCENES OUTSIDE COURT  Outside the courtroom, Imran Khan’s sister, Aleema Khan, was seen in tears after details of his deteriorating eye condition were discussed.  The case has drawn political attention, with leaders of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) present during the proceedings as legal and medical developments continue.  SON BLAMES REGIME, ALLEGES MEDICAL NEGLECT  Imran Khan’s son, Kasim Khan, reacted to the court proceedings in a post on X, alleging that his father’s deteriorating eyesight was the result of prolonged solitary confinement and medical neglect. “We have been informed that my father, Imran Khan, has lost most of the vision in his right eye, with reports indicating only 15% eyesight remains,” Kasim wrote.  He claimed the condition was a consequence of 922 days of solitary confinement, denial of blood tests and lack of proper medical treatment in jail. Kasim further alleged that responsibility lay with the current regime and military leadership, accusing authorities of manipulating the justice system to keep the former prime minister in isolation.  advertisement  Kasim and his brother, Sulaiman, also said they were being denied visas to visit their father as his health deteriorates.  In his statement, Kasim urged human rights organisations, legal institutions and democratic governments to intervene and ensure accountability.    - Ends  Published By: Priyanka Kumari Published On: Feb 12, 2026  Tune In

title: No bail for Rajpal Yadav today, court to hear the case on Monday
authors: New Delhi
text: Actor Rajpal Yadav is currently serving a six-month jail term in a decade-old cheque-bounce case. He surrendered at Delhi's Tihar Jail last week in the case involving nearly Rs 9 crore of repayment. The court didn't give any relief to the actor during the hearing on Thursday, and adjourned the case to Monday, February 16.  The court observed that there were "so many things" that it was not aware of. It also asked the other side to file a response to the bail application. The court also pulled up Yadav by telling him that he didn't honour his commitment, and while they sympathise with the actor, they will have to abide by the law.  "The problem is that I may have sympathy with you, but the law is the law," the judge added. Yadav's counsel said the remaining amount could be deposited in court as security and sought bail, citing a marriage in the family.  What did Rajpal Yadav say before surrendering?  Moments before he surrendered at the Tihar Jail, Yadav shared his ordeal in the cheque-bounce case. He claimed that he had no money and friends, and surrendering was his only option. As the news broke out, the actor, however, received help from his colleagues and friends in the industry.  Speaking to Bollywood Hungama about his situation, Yadav earlier explained his financial difficulties, saying, "Sir, kya karoon? Mere paas paise nahin hain (sir, what to do? I don’t have the money to pay back). Aur koi upaay nahin dikhta (can't see another way out)."  As revealed by his manager, Goldie, Bollywood celebrities, including Salman Khan, Ajay Devgn and others extended financial help. His wife, Radha Yadav, thanked members of the Hindi film industry for helping him amid his financial struggles. The family is confident that the hearing would go in their favour.  Stay tuned for live updates!

title: West Bengal reports 1st Nipah death, 25-year-old nurse succumbs to virus
text: A 25-year-old nurse died on Thursday after battling Nipah virus infection at a private hospital in North 24 Parganas district of, marking the first death from the virus in West Bengal in recent history.  Hospital sources said the nurse, who was among two nursing staff infected with Nipah, had been under treatment for several weeks. While she had recently tested negative for the virus, her condition remained critical.  advertisement  The second infected staff member, a male nurse, was discharged in January after recovering.  The female nurse, however, remained admitted as her health deteriorated. She had been kept in the critical care unit (CCU) for a prolonged period and was put on ventilator support on Wednesday.  She died at around 4 pm on Thursday at the private hospital in Barasat, officials said.  According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), Nipah virus infection is a zoonotic disease transmitted to humans from animals, and can also spread through contaminated food or direct human-to-human contact.  - Ends

title: Kerala High Court grants bail to Rahul Mamkootathil MLA in sexual assault case
text: The Kerala High Court on Thursday granted anticipatory bail to the Palakkad MLA in the first of three alleged sexual assault cases filed against him, effectively securing protection from arrest in all current matters. While the court observed that the allegations did not prima facie establish a case of rape, it imposed several strict conditions for the bail.  The MLA is prohibited from leaving Kerala and must surrender both his passport and mobile phone to the investigating officers. Additionally, he is strictly barred from contacting the complainant or influencing any witnesses. The court has also mandated that he appear before the investigation officers every second Saturday. This legal development provides significant relief to the legislator ahead of the upcoming assembly elections, as it allows him to remain on the ground. However, the court maintained that if an arrest is required, he must be released on bail immediately under the specified conditions, ensuring the investigation continues without his detention.

title: Defeated yet defiant: Harry Brook defends England's spin-playing abilities
text: Here's the full transcript of England captain Harry Brook's press conference after their February 11 match against the West Indies.  [Reporter:]  Harry. Where do you think things went wrong today?  [Harry Brook:]  We probably didn't execute as well as we usually can. We didn't quite execute well enough with the ball and they probably got 15, 20 too many.  [Reporter:]  Do you think it was with the ball? I mean, how did you feel at halfway?  [Harry Brook:]  Well, we thought it was chasable, definitely. We obviously planned for dew and it didn't quite get as dew as we thought, and it didn't quite slide onto the bat as much as we were expecting. But yeah, T20 cricket's such a fickle game and the West Indians are such a powerful side.  [Reporter:]  Six wickets to spin, I think that sort of changed the complexion of the game after the power play. Do you guys struggle against spin in this part of the world?  [Harry Brook:]  No, I don't think so. That series against Sri Lanka showed that. I thought we played spin really well out there. They bowled well; they kept themselves in the game the whole time. Like you said, we lost quite a few wickets in clusters, which never really helps.  [Reporter:]  And just a word on Adil Rashid, he back to his brilliant best after a tough one against Nepal, just shows that he probably wasn't unfazed by what happened on Sunday.  [Harry Brook:]  Yeah, unbelievable. That's the Rash that everybody knows and loves, and his skill and his nous out there was unreal to watch.  [Reporter:]  Harry, yes, no doubt it's the World Cup, but the fact that the points are not carried forward or rather the seedings also don't change in the Super 8s. Does that play on the mind in the preliminary stage when you're playing against the top two teams? Does it actually change the outlook?  [Harry Brook:]  Not really, we've just been trying to take it game by game. And like I said, West Indies have probably played a better game than us there and they deserve the win. And we've just got to focus on the next game now.  [Reporter:]  You mentioned that Sri Lanka series when you did play pretty well against Spin. Does the pressure of a World Cup chase come into things in a situation like that when it didn't go as well?  [Harry Brook:]  One thing I would say is we were probably a little bit careful. Chasing nearly 200 is always a big ask and like I said we didn't think - we thought the pitch would get a little bit better and it'd slide onto the bat a bit more and that didn't happen, but yeah - like I said we were probably a little bit careful, myself included.  [Reporter:]  Is that like your dismissal, maybe Tom's dismissal, like popping catches back rather than... I mean, you've said before, haven't you, you may as well get caught on the boundary rather than in the infield or by the ball, or is that kind of what you mean?  [Harry Brook:]  Well, I'd much rather get caught on the boundary than the way I did today. But yeah, that's part of T20 cricket. He was probably the main threat at that time. So I was just, personally, I was just trying to knock it into the legside and get Sam back on strike.  [Reporter:]  And Joff, an expensive day for him today, probably not at his best on Sunday against Nepal. Any concerns there?  [Harry Brook:]  No, not really. Everybody knows how good Jof is. He'll bounce back for sure. He's bowling rapid and I'm sure he'll execute better in the coming games.  [Reporter:]  A quick turnaround time between now and Scotland, of course now you'll be going to Kolkata, just wanted to know what are the positives that you can take from the two matches you played at the Wankhede? Because, of course, one result did go your way, but it went down the wire, and today, of course, it didn't go your way. What are the positives that you can take forward to Kolkata?  [Harry Brook:]  I think we can take a lot of confidence from not only the Nepal game, but the last T20 in Sri Lanka when they were both tight games. We can take a lot of confidence from them and in the depth with the batting that we have as well, we were stood up in the changing room and we still needed 50 off four overs and we still had faith. So I think we can take a lot of confidence going forward. Obviously, it didn't pay off today, but another day it would work.  [Reporter:]  Just in terms of the playing of spin, what are the things you could do a bit better going forward in the tournament?  [Harry Brook:]  Like I said, I thought we played spin outstanding in Sri Lanka and we just had a bad day today. We didn't manage to get over the line and they bowled well.  [Reporter:]  And you said you got very, you bat very deep. It's almost like you didn't use that line up as much as you could, because you didn't go as hard as you could earlier. Is that how it feels a little bit?  [Reporter:]  That's where it comes back to me saying it's a little, we were a little bit careful. I think with the power that we have at the back end. Like I said, myself included, I feel like I could have potentially taken a risk a little bit earlier knowing that we still had Jacksy, Jamie Overton to come in. And with that power and the depth that we have, we do think that we can chase almost anything. Obviously, today we didn't.  [Reporter:]  Talking about Motie, the left-armer, he bowls orthodox and wrist spin. Does that produce, sort of create extra problems when facing him?  [Harry Brook:]  Well it was a bit obvious that he was only bowling leg spin to the left-handers today. He's a good bowler; he's been a very good bowler for the last few years. I've faced him a lot and he's got a lot of skill. He manages to hit his length consistently.

title: Too late now to say sorry: Norwegian athlete cheats, plays victim, ruins the moment
text: A few days ago, the name Sturla Holm Laegreid may not have struck a chord with many sports enthusiasts around the globe. In the early hours of Wednesday, February 11, those closely following the Winter Olympics would have known him simply as the bronze medallist in the men’s 20-kilometre individual biathlon. By the time the day drew to a close, however, he was known for something entirely different — the Norwegian biathlete who confessed on live television to cheating on his partner.  advertisement  Team Norway had just clinched two biathlon medals, gold and bronze, at the Milan-Cortina Games — a moment filled with pride and emotion. Not long ago, one of the team’s stars, Sivert Guttorm Bakken, had passed away, and the performance was meant to be a tribute to him. The gold medallist, Johan-Olav Botn, reflected that sentiment perfectly, pointing to the sky in remembrance of his fallen teammate.  When it came to Laegreid, similar emotions were expected to surface. After all, this was his first individual Olympic medal, and Norwegian media anticipated the usual post-podium responses — gratitude for family, coaches, or perhaps a special person in his life.  There was someone special that Laegreid chose to mention. And that choice would define his infamy.  Speaking to Norwegian media, just seconds into the interview, Laegreid confessed to cheating on his girlfriend — the “love of his life,” as he called her.  “Six months ago, I met the love of my life. The world’s most beautiful, sweetest person. And three months ago, I made the biggest mistake of my life and cheated on her,” said Laegreid as he burst into tears.  “I’m not quite sure what I’m trying to say by saying this now, but sport has taken a back seat in recent days. I wish I could share this with her.”  At least that last part, he managed — in what was arguably the worst way possible.  From a journalistic standpoint, it was a gold mine. The video went viral. The clicks soared. But when the sporting achievement is stripped away, Laegreid came across as someone who simply could not read the room.  READ THE ROOM, STURLA  First, let’s address why Laegreid was in the wrong, starting with the act itself. Without playing moral compass, cheating is hardly something to be defended — particularly when you describe someone as the “love of your life.” No public confession, however emotional, cleanses that image.  More troubling was how his confession dragged his partner into unwanted global attention. While people attempt many things to reconcile with former partners, emotionally cornering someone through a public platform is not one of them. Laegreid’s partner did not choose this spotlight, and her response made that clear.  advertisement  “I didn't choose to be put in this position, and it's painful to have to endure it,” she told VG. “We've been in contact, and he's aware of my feelings about this.”  Then came the sporting cost.  This was supposed to be a day celebrating Botn’s gold and Norway’s dominance in a sport deeply ingrained in the country’s culture. Instead, the narrative shifted entirely — away from athletic excellence and toward a personal confession framed as a grand romantic gesture.  Laegreid did apologise for stealing the spotlight from Botn and later paid tribute to Bakken, but by then, it felt more like damage control than reflection.  Olympic biathlon gold medallist Johannes Thingnes B¸, now working as an expert with NRK, questioned the timing of the confession.  “It came as a complete surprise. His action was wrong - we saw a repentant lad standing there. Unfortunately, the time, place and timing are all wrong,” B¸ said.  That, ultimately, was Laegreid’s fundamental mistake.  IS LAEGREID WRONG — OR JUST HUMAN?  While B¸ criticised Laegreid’s actions, he also showed empathy.  “With Sturla, the emotions are on the outside of his body. He can’t hide it. I think it just burst out. I don’t know if he had thought in advance that it would happen,” said B¸.  advertisement  Speaking without thinking is something everyone has done. But consider the context Laegreid found himself in — physically exhausted after a gruelling race, emotionally weighed down by personal guilt, and suddenly thrust into the spotlight after winning an Olympic medal.  In that state, restraint is difficult. His own words made that clear.  “My only way to solve it is to tell everything and put everything on the table, and hope that she can still love me. I've done that for her, and now for the whole world. I have nothing to lose. I want to be a good role model, but I have to admit when I make mistakes.”  He later added:  “Of course, now I hope I didn't ruin Johan's day. I don't know if it was the right choice or not, but it was the choice I made. I made the choice to tell the world what I did so maybe there's a chance she will see what she really means to me - maybe not, but I don't want to think I didn't try everything to get her back. I don't want to steal the show. I hope this is just like a day-or-two thing. Then you are an Olympic gold medallist forever.”  advertisement  Not naming his partner — and acknowledging Botn’s moment — may be the only things Laegreid got right on a day of sporting achievement and personal infamy.  He said he wanted to be a role model. And perhaps he became one — not for what to say, but for what not to say, on national television, moments after winning an Olympic medal.  - Ends

title: Needs to grow up: Hardeep Puri tears into Rahul Gandhi over Epstein files charges
text: Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri, whose name surfaced in the court documents and files linked to disgraced US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, launched a sharp attack on Rahul Gandhi for raising the issue in Parliament, saying the Congress leader “needs to grow up”. He accused the Leader of the Opposition of indulging in “politics by innuendo” and said his remarks reflected “streaks of buffoonery”.  advertisement  In an exclusive interview with India Today, Puri said he had personally informed Gandhi about the context in which his name appeared in a limited number of emails among millions of Epstein files documents that have surfaced publicly. He added that had Gandhi read the note, he would not have “made a fool of himself” in Parliament.  “So, this is not about Epstein. This story is about the lack of maturity and the fact that the Leader of the Opposition -- who believes in politics by innuendo and follows a ‘spit and fly’ approach -- hasn’t grown up,” Puri said.  Escalating his attack, Puri remarked that in the civil services there is a provision for voluntary retirement for non-performing officials, adding, “He has not grown up.”  Describing Gandhi’s approach as “politics by innuendo,” Puri accused him of making allegations and then avoiding substantive debate. “If you want to raise an issue, you must do your research and allow the other side to respond. What he does is say something and then run away,” Puri said, adding that Parliament is a forum for informed participation, not insinuation.  “I have always said that the essence of freedom of speech, the essence of democracy, the essence of parliamentary participation is in taking part in a discussion, not by spit and fly,” he said.  Slamming Rahul Gandhi over his criticism of the trade deal with the US -- which he described as a “wholesale surrender” and a “selling out of Bharat Mata” -- the minister said the Congress leader was “jealous that India is doing well, because he does not believe in the aspirations of the people".  “As my colleague and friend Kiren Rijiju said, to allege that the Prime Minister surrendered ‘Koi Maaika Laal abhi paida nahi hua (no one brave enough has been born yet)' to level such a charge against Narendra Modi,” he said, continuing his attack.  The minister further alleged that “Gandhi’s performance displayed elements of buffoonery".  "There are two kinds of politics, one they dedicate their lives to the nation, have no private attachments, no private property, I should have said. And the second, who provide entertainment value through streaks of buffoonery, period," Puri said.  On linking him to Jeffrey Epstein, the minister explained his name appears in only two emails among nearly three million documents that were made public. He said he served as India’s Ambassador to the United States from May 2009 to 2017 and met Epstein four times over eight years in connection with his role as Secretary General of the Independent Commission for Multilateralism (ICM), a project of the International Peace Institute (IPI).  advertisement  "I met hundreds of people every year in my official capacity,” Puri said.  He claimed he was “ambushed” into attending one of the meetings as part of a delegation and said that once concerns about Epstein became clearer, he and others distanced themselves.  Puri also rejected suggestions that his interactions were inappropriate. Referring to an email exchange cited in media reports, he said it involved discussions on investment opportunities in India and advice to LinkedIn founder Reid Hoffman about expanding in Indian languages.  The minister maintained that the issue had been publicly available for months and alleged that Gandhi chose to raise it without examining the facts.  - Ends  Published By: Ajmal Published On: Feb 12, 2026  Tune In

title: Benvuento Italy: Azurri make World Cup history, stun Nepal at Wankhede
text: Brief scores: Italy (124/0 in 12.4 ov) beat Nepal (123 in 20 ov) by 10 wickets in Mumbai in a Group C match.  ITA vs NEP T20 WORLD CUP 2026: HIGHLIGHTS | SCORECARD  Who would have thought Italy’s first World Cup triumph in 2026 would come not on the football field, but at a cricket World Cup? In a year when the Italy football team are in danger of missing the FIFA World Cup for the third consecutive edition, their cricket team soared, keeping the national flag flying high on the world stage.  advertisement  On Thursday, Italy reigned supreme at Wankhede Stadium, claiming their first-ever victory in T20 World Cup history. The Azzurri stunned Nepal by 10 wickets in a dominant Group C clash at the iconic Mumbai venue—a victory that spoke of belief, courage, and sheer determination.  Nepal came in as favourites, riding the high of nearly toppling the 2022 champions England and cheered on by a roaring sea of red. Yet Italy were fearless. They didn’t just win—they dominated, proving to the world that their triumph was no accident. The Azzurri had arrived.  Italy’s journey in the tournament began harshly with a 73-run loss to Scotland, during which skipper Wayne Madsen injured his shoulder. It could have been a setback too heavy to overcome. But instead, Italy embraced a fearless approach, refusing to let adversity define them.  Against all odds, they rose. Joe Burns, their qualifying hero, was absent, and Madsen’s injury threatened to derail their hopes. On paper, they looked fragile—but on the field, they were unstoppable. Every run and every delivery revealed hearts that refused to falter and spirits that refused to bend.  Harry Manenti led with calm authority, guiding Italy as they raced through Nepal’s 124-run target, finishing the chase with 44 balls to spare. Each shot, each run, sent a clear message: the Azzurri were here, bold, fearless, and ready to make history.  KALUGAMAGE, MANENTI ROCK NEPAL  After being asked to bat first, Nepal lost the early wicket of Kushal Bhurtel, but Aasif Sheikh and skipper Rohit Paudel steadied the innings, helping Nepal score 45 runs in the powerplay. However, from that point, Italy’s spin duo of Crishan Kalugamage and Ben Manenti made the Nepalese batters work hard for every run.  Paudel, who scored 23, and Aasif Sheikh, who made 20, fell in quick succession as Kalugamage and Manenti undid all their early efforts. Dipendra Singh Airee, who scored 17, and Aarif Sheikh, who made 27, then tried to steady the innings, putting on 43 runs for the third wicket, with Nepal standing strong at 93 for 3 in the 14th over.  advertisement  From there, Nepal’s innings collapsed like a house of cards, being bowled out for 123 in 19.3 overs. Kalugamage was the pick of the bowlers, finishing with 4 overs, 18 runs, and 3 wickets, while Manenti took 2 wickets. Ali Hasan, JJ Smuts, and Jaspreet Singh claimed 1 wicket each, helping Italy dominate the innings and set up a historic victory.  MOSCA BROTHERS MAKE HAY  Italy’s run chase was powered by the Mosca brothers, Anthony and Justin, who ensured Nepal never had a chance to stage a comeback. Once they scored 68 runs in the powerplay, the outcome was all but decided, as the Moscas batted with relentless authority.  Their fifty-run partnership came off just four overs, showcasing their dominance. Justin Mosca was the first to reach his fifty, achieving the milestone off 37 balls. He went on to remain unbeaten on 66 from 44 balls, striking five fours and three sixes.  Anthony Mosca, the aggressor, reached his fifty off only 28 balls. Together, the duo brought up a century partnership in 65 balls, taking Italy closer to victory. Anthony finished not out on 62 from 32 balls, hitting three fours and six sixes, and struck the winning run.  advertisement  For Nepal, Dipendra Singh Airee bowled tightly and tried to keep the batters in check, but apart from him, the other bowlers leaked runs at an alarming rate, unable to contain Italy’s fearless assault.
